TABATABAI:2:186#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads divine nearness as absolute: true divine ownership makes humans His servants and brings Him nearer than anything; the cited verses also describe this nearness.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r1.anchor: إن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه الأنفال 24، والقلب هو النفس المدركة

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r2.claim: Because God’s dominion and encompassing rule cover every possibility, He can answer any creature’s prayer and remove its need through giving and action.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r2.anchor: أن لله سبحانه أن يجيب أي دعاء دعى به أحد من خلقه ويرفع بالاعطاء والتصرف حاجته

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r3.speaker: اليهود
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r3.claim: The Jews hold that after God created things and fixed their decrees, control passed from Him; thus there is no abrogation, badāʾ, or response to prayer.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r3.anchor: لا كما يقوله اليهود إن الله لما خلق الأشياء وقدر التقادير تم الأمر، وخرج زمام التصرف الجديد من يده

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r4.speaker: القدرية
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r4.claim: The Qadariyya say God has no agency in human actions; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this denial of divine sovereignty over acts.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r4.anchor: ولا كما يقوله جماعة من هذه الأمة أن لا صنع لله في أفعال عباده وهم القدرية

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r5.claim: A Prophetic report transmitted by both schools calls the Qadariyya the Magians of this community.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r5.anchor: فيما رواه الفريقان من قوله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم القدرية مجوس هذه الأمة

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r6.claim: God alone owns absolutely; created things possess only what He grants and permits, and what He neither wills nor permits cannot occur despite human effort.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r6.anchor: بل الملك لله سبحانه على الإطلاق ولا يملك شيء شيئا إلا بتمليك منه سبحانه وإذن

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r7.claim: The verse gives both the rule of answered prayer and its cause: people are God's servants, so He is near them, and His nearness grounds His unrestricted response.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r7.anchor: فكون الداعين عبادا لله تعالى هو الموجب لقربه منهم، وقربه منهم هو الموجب لإجابته المطلقة لدعائهم

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r8.claim: The condition “when he calls Me” requires the caller to possess the stated quality genuinely, as in listening to an adviser when he truly advises or honoring a person who truly knows.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r8.anchor: فإن قولنا اصغ إلى قول الناصح إذا نصحك أو أكرم العالم إذا كان عالما

TABATABAI:2:186#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r9.claim: The promise applies to a genuine caller whose innate knowledge and desire unite heart and tongue; prayer is what the heart bears and the tongue of natural disposition voices, not words used in jest or falsehood.
TABATABAI:2:186#2/r9.anchor: فإن حقيقة الدعاء والسؤال هو الذي يحمله القلب ويدعو به لسان الفطرة، دون ما يأتي به اللسان

TABATABAI:2:186#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r1.claim: The uncounted blessings people “asked” for in 14:34, and all beings’ daily asking in 55:29, are requests made by innate need rather than spoken words; 55:29 makes the point clearer.
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r1.anchor: يسأله من في السماوات والأرض كل يوم هو في شأن

TABATABAI:2:186#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r2.claim: A request made by natural disposition to God does not miss its answer; an apparently unanswered prayer must lack either genuine asking or exclusive reliance on God.
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r2.anchor: فالسؤال الفطري من الله سبحانه لا يتخطى الإجابة

TABATABAI:2:186#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r3.claim: One failure is that the person has not truly asked: ignorance may lead someone to request what cannot happen or what they would not want if they knew its reality, as with asking for cure rather than a dead person's return to life.
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r3.anchor: فإما أن يكون لم يتحقق هناك دعاء، وإنما التبس الأمر على الداعي التباسا

TABATABAI:2:186#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r4.claim: Another failure is a heart attached to ordinary causes or imagined powers as sufficient or effective; despite verbal invocation, the person has not truly and exclusively asked God.
TABATABAI:2:186#3/r4.anchor: وإما أن السؤال متحقق لكن لا من الله وحده كمن يسأل الله حاجة من حوائجه وقلبه متعلق بالأسباب العادية

TABATABAI:2:186#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r1.claim: The passages in 6:40–41 and 6:63–64 show that hardship strips away imagined partners and causes, returning people to innate monotheism; in ease they again attribute efficacy to causes and forget God.
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r1.anchor: تبين له أن لا منجح لحاجته ولا مجيب لمسألته إلا الله

TABATABAI:2:186#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r2.claim: In 40:60, “My worship” means calling upon God: the verse invites prayer and promises a response while explicitly naming prayer as worship.
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r2.anchor: والآية تدعو إلى الدعاء وتعد بالإجابة وتزيد على ذلك حيث تسمي الدعاء عبادة بقولها عن عبادتي أي عن دعائي

TABATABAI:2:186#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r3.claim: The threat of Hell for abandoning prayer concerns abandoning worship altogether, not merely one branch of worship; this shows that prayer is the root of worship.
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r3.anchor: والوعيد بالنار إنما هو على ترك العبادة رأسا لا على ترك بعض أقسامه دون بعض فأصل العبادة دعاء

TABATABAI:2:186#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r4.claim: Other passages depict prayer through fear and hope, earnest calling, hidden invocation, and the response to believers who do good; they illuminate this verse’s subject.
TABATABAI:2:186#4/r4.anchor: وادعوه خوفا وطمعا إن رحمة الله قريب من المحسنين

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r1.claim: The prayer passages just cited contain prayer’s pillars and etiquette; their central requirement is sincerity, with heart and tongue aligned, detachment from every cause besides God, and reliance on Him.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r1.anchor: وهي تشتمل على أركان الدعاء وآداب الداعي، وعمدتها الإخلاص في دعائه تعالى وهو مواطات القلب اللسان

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r2.claim: The final clause follows from God being near, unobstructed by anything, and caring for His servants and their requests: they should accept His invitation, turn to Him, and believe He is near and responsive.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r2.anchor: فليستجيبوا له في هذه الدعوة، وليقبلوا إليه، وليؤمنوا به في هذا النعت، وليوقنوا بأنه قريب مجيب

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet and transmitted by both schools says that prayer is the believer’s weapon.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فيما رواه الفريقان الدعاء سلاح المؤمن

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r4.speaker: الله تعالى
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r4.claim: In a sacred hadith addressed to Moses, God tells him to ask for every need, even fodder for his sheep and salt for his dough.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r4.anchor: وفي عدة الداعي في الحديث القدسي يا موسى سلني كل ما تحتاج إليه حتى علف شاتك وملح عجينك

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r5.claim: Al-Makārim reports that the Prophet called prayer better than Quran recitation, citing 25:77; the same saying is also reported from al-Bāqir and al-Ṣādiq.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r5.anchor: وفي المكارم عنه عليه السلام الدعاء أفضل من قراءة القرآن

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r6.claim: A report in ʿUddat al-dāʿī says God revealed to a prophet that He will disappoint whoever hopes in another, since relief and the open door of response are in His hands.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r6.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:2:186#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r7.speaker: الله تعالى
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r7.claim: A sacred report says one who relies on a creature apart from God will be denied response, while one who relies on God receives provision, response, gifts, and forgiveness.
TABATABAI:2:186#5/r7.anchor: ما من مخلوق يعتصم بمخلوق دوني إلا قطعت أسباب السماوات وأسباب الأرض من دونه

TABATABAI:2:186#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r1.claim: The preceding reports call for sincerity in prayer; they do not deny created causes, which God appoints as intermediaries rather than independent sources of effect.
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r1.anchor: وما اشتمل عليه الحديثان هو الإخلاص في الدعاء، وليس إبطالا لسببية الأسباب الوجودية التي جعلها الله تعالى وسائل متوسطة

TABATABAI:2:186#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r2.claim: Innate awareness recognizes a true, unfailing giver behind needs and also knows apparent causes may fail; therefore one should not rely on a visible cause as though separate from the real source.
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r2.anchor: فإنه يشعر بفطرته أن لحاجته سببا معطيا لا يتخلف عنه فعله،

TABATABAI:2:186#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r3.claim: When a requested need is fulfilled, the request has in truth reached God through causes; asking a visible cause as if it alone sufficed is an imaginative construction, not innate awareness.
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r3.anchor: فإذا سأل أو طلب شيئا من حوائجه فوقع ما طلبه كشف ذلك أنه سأل ربه واتصل حاجته

TABATABAI:2:186#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r4.claim: Innate desire can oppose a person's words or imagined wishes, like the sick child who rejects bitter medicine while naturally seeking health; the natural order is sound, whereas imagination often errs, so the reports concern the heart’s true request.
TABATABAI:2:186#6/r4.anchor: فالصبي المريض إذا عرض عليه الدواء المر امتنع من شربه وأخذ بالبكاء وهو يريد الصحة،

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r1.claim: The Prophet teaches believers to pray while certain of the response.

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r2.claim: A sacred hadith says God is as His servant thinks of Him, so the servant should expect good.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r2.anchor: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي، فلا يظن بي إلا خيرا

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r3.claim: Prayer with despair or hesitation shows that the person is not truly asking; the source also reports a prohibition on praying for what cannot be.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r3.anchor: أقول وذلك أن الدعاء مع اليأس أو التردد يكشف عن عدم السؤال في الحقيقة كما مر،

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r4.claim: The Prophet urges turning to God in needs and distress, calls prayer the marrow of worship, and says its answer may be immediate, deferred to the afterlife, or take the form of expiation, unless the request is sinful.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r4.anchor: افزعوا إلى الله في حوائجكم، والجأوا إليه في ملماتكم، وتضرعوا إليه وادعوه

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r5.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r5.claim: In his testament to al-Ḥusayn, ʿAlī says God placed the keys to His treasures in the servant’s hands by permitting requests, so supplication opens the doors of blessings and mercy.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r5.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة في وصية له عليه السلام لابنه الحسين عليه السلام ثم جعل في يديك مفاتيح خزائنه بما أذن لك فيه من مسألته

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r6.claim: ʿAlī’s phrase “the gift is according to intention” means the response matches what the heart truly intends, not necessarily the wording that the tongue displays.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r6.anchor: قوله فإن العطية على قدر النية يريد عليه السلام به إن الاستجابة تطابق الدعوة فما سأله السائل منه تعالى على حسب ما عقد عليه حقيقة ضميره

TABATABAI:2:186#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r7.claim: Apparent delay, a better worldly or afterlife substitute, or diversion to what suits the petitioner are still answers matching the real request; a believer may unknowingly ask for what would harm faith and receive what benefits the afterlife.
TABATABAI:2:186#7/r7.anchor: وقد بين عليه السلام بها عدة من الموارد التي يتراءى فيها تخلف الاستجابة عن الدعوة ظاهرا

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r1.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r1.claim: Al-Bāqir says God is too generous to return hands raised in prayer empty, and instructs the petitioner to wipe the hands over the head and face, or in another report over face and chest.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r1.anchor: وفي عدة الداعي عن الباقر عليه السلام ما بسط عبد يده إلى الله عز وجل إلا استحيى الله أن يردها صفرا

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r2.speaker: سلمان وجابر وعبد الله بن عمر وأنس بن مالك وابن أبي مغيث
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r2.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr cites eight Prophetic reports through several Companions, all of which mention raising hands in prayer.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r2.anchor: عن عدة من الصحابة كسلمان، وجابر، وعبد الله بن عمر

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the claim that raising hands implies God is in the sky and amounts to anthropomorphism; he calls denial of the gesture a mistaken argument.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r3.anchor: فلا معنى لإنكار بعضهم رفع اليدين بالدعاء معللا بأنه من التجسيم إذ رفع اليدين إلى السماء إيماء إلى إنه تعالى فيها

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r4.claim: Physical worship gives bodily form to inward orientation and transcendent truths; this is necessary to bodily worship, and supplication similarly embodies the heart’s humble request.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r4.anchor: فإن حقيقة جميع العبادات البدنية هي تنزيل المعنى القلبي والتوجه الباطني إلى موطن الصورة

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r5.claim: Reports transmitted by al-Ṭūsī and in ʿUddat al-dāʿī say the Prophet raised his hands when imploring God, as a beggar stretches them for food.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r5.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يرفع يديه إذا ابتهل ودعا كما يستطعم المسكين

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r6.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r6.claim: ʿAlī corrects a man who sought refuge from “trial”: wealth and children themselves are called a trial in 64:15, so he should seek refuge from misleading trials instead.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r6.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام أنه سمع رجلا يقول اللهم أني أعوذ بك من الفتنة، قال عليه السلام أراك تتعوذ من مالك وولدك

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r7.claim: This report illustrates that a word’s right meaning is established by its usage in revelation; the source notes similar cases concerning “part” and “much.”
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r7.anchor: وفيها أن الحق في معنى كل لفظ هو الذي ورد منه في كلامه

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r8.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says God does not answer a prayer made with an inattentive heart.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r8.anchor: وفي عدة الداعي عن الصادق عليه السلام إن الله لا يستجيب دعاء بظهر قلب ساه

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r9.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r9.claim: ʿAlī says God does not accept a prayer from a heedless heart.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r9.anchor: وفي العدة أيضا عن علي عليه السلام لا يقبل الله دعاء قلب لاه

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r10.claim: Heedlessness and distraction prevent the reality of prayer and petition from taking place.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r10.anchor: والسر فيه عدم تحقق حقيقة الدعاء والمسألة في السهو واللهو

TABATABAI:2:186#8/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r11.speaker: الله عز وجل
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r11.claim: A Torah saying in al-Rāwandī’s Dawʿāt warns that one who prays against an oppressor may himself face the prayers of those he has wronged; God may answer both sides or defer both until Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:2:186#8/r11.anchor: وفي دعوات الراوندي في التوراة يقول الله عز وجل للعبد إنك متى ظللت تدعوني على عبد من عبيدي

TABATABAI:2:186#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r1.claim: One who asks revenge for another’s wrongdoing accepts the same standard for every comparable case; if that petitioner has wronged someone, the request applies to him too, while unwillingness to accept that result shows the prayer is not genuine.
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r1.anchor: فإذا دعا على من ظلمه بالانتقام فقد دعا عليه لأجل ظلمه فهو راض بالانتقام من الظالم،

TABATABAI:2:186#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r2.claim: The principle is illustrated by 17:11: a person may call for evil just as he calls for good, because the human being is hasty.
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r2.anchor: ويدع الإنسان بالشر دعائه بالخير وكان الإنسان عجولا

TABATABAI:2:186#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Abū Dharr to preserve God’s commands, recognize Him in ease, ask and seek help only from Him, and notes that no creature can give what God has not written for a person.
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لأبي ذر

TABATABAI:2:186#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r4.claim: “Know God in ease and He will know you in hardship” means invoke Him while things are easy; one who forgets God then treats causes as independent and only acknowledges lordship conditionally in distress.
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r4.anchor: تعرف إلى الله في الرخاء يعرفك في الشدة يعني ادع الله في الرخاء ولا تنسه حتى يستجيب دعاءك في الشدة

TABATABAI:2:186#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r5.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says one who makes supplication before affliction will be answered when it comes; the angels recognize that familiar voice and do not bar it from heaven, unlike an unfamiliar voice.
TABATABAI:2:186#9/r5.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال عليه السلام من تقدم في الدعاء أستجيب له إذا نزل البلاء

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r1.claim: The warning “they forgot God, so He forgot them” in 9:67 supports the point; this does not contradict reports that prayer is not rejected in complete severance, since ordinary hardship is not total severance.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r1.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا ما ورد أن الدعاء لا يرد مع الانقطاع،

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r2.claim: Asking and seeking help from God means relying on Him as the true source: ordinary causes have only the limited, God-given role of pathways and intermediaries, so exclusive reliance on them is misplaced.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r2.anchor: فإن هذه الأسباب العادية التي بين أيدينا إنما سببيتها محدودة على ما قدر الله لها من الحد لا على ما يتراءى من استقلالها

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r3.claim: This teaching does not abolish created causes: a person asks with the heart, speaks with the tongue, and employs bodily organs, just as giving, seeing, and hearing require a hand, eye, and ear.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r3.anchor: كيف والداعي يريد ما يسأله بالقلب، ويسأل ما يريده باللسان ويستعين على ذلك بأركان وجوده وكل ذلك أسباب

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r4.claim: Depending on a cause as though it acted independently is like attaching one’s heart to a person’s hand or eye while forgetting the person who acts through them.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r4.anchor: ومن ركن إلى سبب من دون الله سبحانه وتعالى كان كمن تعلق قلبه بيد الإنسان في إعطائه أو بعينه في نظرها

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r5.claim: God’s unrestricted power and necessary freedom remain intact: the limits described concern the particular act and its conditions, not the agent, just as human ability to give, see, and hear is expressed through organs.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك تقييدا للقدرة الإلهية غير المتناهية ولا سلبا للاختيار الواجبي،

TABATABAI:2:186#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r6.claim: A particular act of creating Zayd depends on parents, time, place, conditions, and absence of obstacles; it is the effect, not the divine agent, that depends on these causes.
TABATABAI:2:186#10/r6.anchor: فزيد مثلا وهو فعل لله هو الإنسان الذي ولده فلان وفلانة في زمان كذا ومكان كذا وعند وجود شرائط كذا وارتفاع موانع كذا

TABATABAI:2:186#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r1.claim: The statement that the pen has recorded what will occur explains why one should ask God: events are determined by Him, while His sovereignty and will remain active and effective at every moment.
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r1.anchor: والمعنى أن الحوادث مكتوبة مقدرة من عند الله تعالى لا تأثير لسبب من الأسباب فيها حقيقة،

TABATABAI:2:186#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r2.speaker: اليهود وغيرهم
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r2.claim: An objection says the requested need is either already decreed, and therefore necessary, or not decreed, and therefore impossible; either way prayer cannot affect it.
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r2.anchor: أن الحاجة المدعو لها إما أن تكون مقضية مقدرة أو لا،

TABATABAI:2:186#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r3.claim: Predetermination does not make a thing independent of its causes; prayer itself is one cause, so when it occurs its effect can occur. This is what the reports mean by saying prayer is part of decree.
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r3.anchor: والجواب أن فرض تقدير وجود الشيء لا يوجب استغنائه عن أسباب وجوده،

TABATABAI:2:186#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says that nothing averts decree except prayer.
TABATABAI:2:186#11/r4.anchor: ففي البحار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r1.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r1.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says prayer can avert a decree even after it has been firmly established.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r1.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام الدعاء يرد القضاء بعد ما أبرم إبراما

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن موسى عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r2.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā urges prayer because it averts a decreed calamity even when its implementation is all that remains.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r2.anchor: وعن أبي الحسن موسى عليه السلام عليكم بالدعاء فإن الدعاء والطلب إلى الله عز وجل يرد البلاء

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r3.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq again says prayer averts a firmly decreed outcome and calls it the key to mercy and success in every need; what is with God is attained only by prayer.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r3.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام إن الدعاء يرد القضاء المبرم وقد أبرم إبراما

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r4.claim: These reports point to persistence: repeatedly pursuing a sincere intention purifies it.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r4.anchor: أقول وفيها إشارة إلى الإصرار وهو من محققات الدعاء، فإن كثرة الإتيان بالقصد يوجب صفائه

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r5.speaker: اسماعيل بن همام عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r5.claim: A single private prayer by a servant equals seventy public prayers.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r5.anchor: وعن اسماعيل بن همام عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام دعوة العبد سرا دعوة واحدة تعدل سبعين دعوة علانية

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r6.claim: Keeping prayer private protects the sincerity of the request.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r6.anchor: أقول وفيها إشارة إلى إخفاء الدعاء وإسراره فإنه أحفظ لإخلاص الطلب

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r7.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r7.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says prayer remains veiled until the petitioner invokes blessings upon Muḥammad and his family.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r7.anchor: وفي المكارم عن الصادق عليه السلام لا يزال الدعاء محجوبا حتى يصلي على محمد وآل محمد

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r8.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says one who presents forty believers before praying will be answered.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r8.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام أيضا، من قدم أربعين من المؤمنين ثم دعا أستجيب له

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r9.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r9.claim: Asked why “Call Me and I will answer” seemed unfulfilled, al-Ṣādiq says to obey God and follow the proper form: praise and glorify Him, recall and thank His blessings, bless Muḥammad and his family, confess sins, and seek forgiveness.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r9.anchor: وعن الصادق عليه السلام أيضا - وقد قال له رجل من أصحابه إني لأجد آيتين

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r10.claim: In the same exchange, al-Ṣādiq explains that God replaces money only when it is lawfully earned and rightly spent; each dirham spent that way is replaced.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r10.anchor: قال لو أن أحدكم اكتسب المال من حله وأنفق في حقه لم ينفق درهما إلا اخلف الله عليه

TABATABAI:2:186#12/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r11.claim: The reported etiquettes of prayer help bring a servant closer to the true reality of prayer and petition.
TABATABAI:2:186#12/r11.anchor: أقول والوجه في هذه الأحاديث الواردة في آداب الدعاء ظاهرة فإنها تقرب العبد من حقيقة الدعاء والمسألة

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r1.claim: The passage cites a saying that when God wills to answer a servant, He opens supplication for him.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r1.anchor: إن الله إذا أراد أن يستجيب لعبد أذن له في الدعاء

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that whoever is granted an opening for supplication is granted the gates of mercy.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عمر أيضا عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r3.claim: A variant of the Ibn Umar report says that an opening for supplication opens the gates of Paradise.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عمر أيضا عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r4.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r4.claim: Reports through the Imams of the Prophet’s Household say that whoever is given supplication is given its answer; al-Tabataba'i says this follows from the prior discussion.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r4.anchor: مروي من طرق أئمة أهل البيت أيضا من أعطي الدعاء أعطي الإجابة

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r5.claim: Mu'adh ibn Jabal transmits the Prophet's saying that true knowledge of God would make mountains move through one's supplication.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r6.claim: Ignorance of God's station and reliance on causes lead people to confine effects to customary causes, even when they treat causes only as necessary intermediaries.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r6.anchor: الجهل بمقام الحق وسلطان الربوبية والركون إلى الأسباب يوجب الإذعان بحقيقة التأثير للأسباب وقصر المعلولات على عللها المعهودة وأسبابها العادية

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r7.claim: Even people who deny that ordinary causes act by themselves may assume their mediation is indispensable; al-Tabataba'i says this assumption conflicts with God's complete sovereignty.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r7.anchor: اعتقدنا بأن السير واسطة والله سبحانه وتعالى هو المؤثر هناك لكن يبقى الاعتقاد بتعين الوساطة

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r8.claim: Causation and the mediation of causes are real, but neither reason nor revelation confines events to their ordinary causes; only intrinsic impossibilities remain unattainable.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r8.anchor: توسط الأسباب بين الله سبحانه وبين مسبباتها حق لا مناص عنه

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r9.claim: Knowing God means accepting that supplication can bring about customary impossibilities that are not intrinsically impossible; the main prophetic miracles are answered prayers.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r9.anchor: ما ليس بمحال ذاتي من كل ما تحيله العادة فإن الدعاء مستجاب فيه كما أن العمدة من معجزات الأنبياء راجعة إلى استجابة الدعوة

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r10.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r10.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Ja'far al-Sadiq's gloss that responding and believing mean knowing God can grant what they ask.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r10.anchor: في تفسير العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام في قوله تعالى فليستجيبوا لي وليؤمنوا بي يعلمون أني أقدر أن أعطيهم ما يسألوني

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r11.claim: Al-Majma' reports Abu Abd Allah's gloss that belief means being certain God can grant what people ask of Him.
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r11.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام إنه قال

TABATABAI:2:186#13/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:186#13/r12.claim: Al-Majma' reports Abu Abd Allah's gloss that guidance means reaching and being guided to the truth.

TABRISI:2:186/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r1.claim: Ajāba and istajāba both mean to answer; a couplet uses them in the same sense. Al-Mubarrad distinguishes them, saying istijāba implies acquiescence while ijāba does not.

TABRISI:2:186/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r2.claim: The root j-w-b means cutting through: one traverses a land or pierces darkness; answering cuts through a question that is suspended between yes and no.
TABRISI:2:186/r2.anchor: وأصله من الجوب وهو القطع يقال جاب البلاد يجوبها جوبا إذا قطعها

TABRISI:2:186/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r3.claim: The author treats jāba, obedience, and capacity as verbal nouns; answering a question is called a response, and clouds clearing is injiāb.
TABRISI:2:186/r3.anchor: والصحيح أن الجابة والطاعة والطاقة ونحوها أسماء بمعنى المصادر

TABRISI:2:186/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r4.claim: Rushd is the opposite of error; the word has two verb forms, and rashīd describes someone soundly guided. The root means attaining good and irshād is guidance toward it.
TABRISI:2:186/r4.anchor: والرشد نقيض الغي رشد يرشد رشدا ورشد يرشد رشدا ورجل رشيد

TABRISI:2:186/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r5.claim: Idhā is a temporal adverb for the implied command Tell them, as indicated by fa-innī qarīb. It cannot be governed by qarīb or ujību because an inna predicate cannot govern outside its clause; ujību is a second predicate of inna.
TABRISI:2:186/r5.anchor: إذا ظرف زمان للفعل الذي يدل عليه

TABRISI:2:186/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:186/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a questioner asked the Prophet whether their Lord was near, so they could whisper to Him, or distant, so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
TABRISI:2:186/r6.anchor: روي عن الحسن أن سائلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه

TABRISI:2:186/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r7.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:186/r7.claim: Qatāda says the verse answered people who asked the Prophet how they should supplicate.
TABRISI:2:186/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة نزلت جوابا لقوم سألوا النبي كيف ندعوا

TABRISI:2:186/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r8.claim: The mention of supplication follows the discussion of fasting and its relation to prayer and God's response.
TABRISI:2:186/r8.anchor: لما ذكر سبحانه الصوم عقبه بذكر الدعاء ومكانه منه وإجابته إياه

TABRISI:2:186/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r9.claim: The question most likely concerns God's attribute, not an action, since the answer says He is near; an implied say introduces the reply.
TABRISI:2:186/r9.anchor: الأقرب أن يكون السؤال عن صفته سبحانه لا عن فعله

TABRISI:2:186/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r10.claim: God has no place: if He were located somewhere, He could not be near to everyone who addresses Him.
TABRISI:2:186/r10.anchor: فدل بهذا على أنه سبحانه لا مكان له إذ لو كان له مكان لم يكن قريبا

TABRISI:2:186/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:186/r11.claim: One interpretation takes near to mean that God answers a supplicant quickly, since nearness and speed are related.
TABRISI:2:186/r11.anchor: وقيل معناه إني سريع الإجابة إلى دعاء الداعي لأن السريع والقريب متقاربان

TABRISI:2:186/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:186/r12.claim: Another interpretation says God hears an invoker as a nearby person hears them; nearness of distance itself is impossible for God because it belongs to created beings situated in a place.
TABRISI:2:186/r12.anchor: وقيل معناه إني أسمع دعاء الداعي كما يسمعه القريب المسافة منهم

TABRISI:2:186/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186/r13.claim: The promise of answering is clear in meaning.

TABRISI:2:186/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:2:186/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains the imperative as answering God in response to what He has called them to do.
TABRISI:2:186/r14.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: معناه فليجيبوني فيما دعوتهم إليه

TABRISI:2:186/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r15.speaker: المبرد والسراج
TABRISI:2:186/r15.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Sarrāj explain it as seeking the truth by conforming to what God commands and forbids.
TABRISI:2:186/r15.anchor: وقال المبرد والسراج: معناه فليذهبوا للحق بطلب موافقة ما أمرتهم به

TABRISI:2:186/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r16.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:186/r16.claim: Mujāhid explains it as responding to God through obedience.
TABRISI:2:186/r16.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معناه فليستجيبوا لي بالطاعة

TABRISI:2:186/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:186/r17.claim: Another interpretation takes the command to mean let them supplicate to Me.

TABRISI:2:186#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:186#2/r1.claim: The Prophet calls the person who cannot supplicate the most incapable and the person who withholds greeting the most miserly.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r1.anchor: أعجز الناس من عجز عن الدعاء وأبخل الناس من بخل بالسلام

TABRISI:2:186#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186#2/r2.claim: Belief here means affirming everything God revealed.

TABRISI:2:186#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:186#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh explains belief as recognizing that God can grant what they request.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله أنه قال: وليؤمنوا بي

TABRISI:2:186#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186#2/r4.claim: They may find the truth and be guided to it.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r4.anchor: أي لعلهم يصيبون الحق ويهتدون إليه

TABRISI:2:186#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186#2/r5.claim: God answers supplication in a manner consistent with wisdom: the request must benefit the person's religion and harm neither the supplicant nor another; God grants it when beneficial and delays it when delay is better.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r5.anchor: ليس أحد يدعو الله على ما توجبه الحكمة إلا أجابه الله فإن الداعي إذا دعاه يجب أن يسأل ما فيه صلاح له في دينه

TABRISI:2:186#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:186#2/r6.claim: Supplication remains meaningful even when wisdom determines the outcome: it is worship expressing humility and submission, and a requested event may become beneficial only after the supplication.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r6.anchor: أن الدعاء عبادة في نفسها يعبد الله سبحانه بها لما في ذلك من إظهار الخضوع والانقياد

TABRISI:2:186#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r7.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:186#2/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports the Prophet saying that a Muslim's prayer without sin or severing kinship receives one of three outcomes: prompt fulfillment, a reward saved for the afterlife, or equivalent harm averted. The Companions ask if they should pray more, and he answers that God is more generous.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r7.anchor: ما من مسلم دعا الله سبحانه بدعوة ليس فيها قطيعة رحم ولا إثم

TABRISI:2:186#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:2:186#2/r8.claim: Anas ibn Mālik's version gives the response as God being more generous and better, repeated three times.

TABRISI:2:186#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r9.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:186#2/r9.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the Prophet saying God may defer a beloved servant's request because He loves hearing the servant's voice, but quickly grant a sincere request from a servant He dislikes because He hates hearing that voice.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن جابر بن عبد الله قال قال رسول الله:

TABRISI:2:186#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r10.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:2:186#2/r10.claim: The Commander of the Faithful says an answer may be delayed to increase the supplicant's reward and make the eventual gift more abundant.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r10.anchor: وروي عن أمير المؤمنين ع أنه قال: ربما أخرت عن العبد

TABRISI:2:186#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:186#2/r11.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
TABRISI:2:186#2/r11.claim: Asked why prayers go unanswered, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham says people know God but disobey, know the Prophet but neglect his Sunna, know the Quran but do not act on it, fail to thank blessings or seek Paradise and flee Hell, agree with Satan, neglect preparation for death, fail to learn from the dead, and occupy themselves with others' faults.
TABRISI:2:186#2/r11.anchor: وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم: ما بالنا ندعو الله سبحانه

THALABI:v2p74/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p74/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Umar ibn al-Khattab and his Companions having intercourse with their wives on Ramadan nights; their story will follow later.
THALABI:v2p74/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأصحابه حين أصابوا من أهاليهم في ليالي شهر رمضان

THALABI:v2p74/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p74/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet asked how God could hear their supplication when the sky was five hundred years away and each heaven was that thick; then the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v2p74/r3.anchor: كيف يسمع ربنا دعاؤنا وأنت تزعم إن بيننا وبين السماء مسيرة خمسمائة عام

THALABI:v2p74/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p74/r4.claim: Hasan says the Companions asked the Prophet where their Lord was, and the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v2p74/r4.anchor: سأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رسول الله أين ربنا؟ فأنزل الله هذه الآية

THALABI:v2p74/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r5.speaker: قتادة وعطاء
THALABI:v2p74/r5.claim: Qatada and ʿAta say that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked how and when to call upon God, and this verse answered them.
THALABI:v2p74/r5.anchor: قال قتادة وعطاء: لما نزلت وقال ربكم: ادعوني أستجب لكم

THALABI:v2p74/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p74/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says Companions asked whether God was near enough for private speech or far away; the Prophet asked God, and the verse came down.
THALABI:v2p74/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك: سأل بعض الصحابة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v2p74/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v2p74/r7.claim: Ahl al-maʿānī see an ellipsis in the address and take nearness to mean nearness in knowledge.
THALABI:v2p74/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: فيه إضمار كأنه فعل هم وما علمهم أفي قريب منهم بالعلم

THALABI:v2p74/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r8.speaker: أهل الإشارة
THALABI:v2p74/r8.claim: Ahl al-ishāra say the intermediary is omitted to manifest divine power.
THALABI:v2p74/r8.anchor: وقال أهل الإشارة: رفع الواسطة إظهارا للقدرة

THALABI:v2p74/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p74/r9.claim: For God, answering is giving; for a servant, responding to God is obedience. Ajāba and istajāba can both mean answer.
THALABI:v2p74/r9.anchor: فليستجيبوا فليجيبوا لي بالطاعة يقال أجاب واستجاب بمعنى واحد

THALABI:v2p74/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r10.speaker: أبو رجاء الخراساني
THALABI:v2p74/r10.claim: Abu Raja al-Khurasani reads the phrase as let them call on Me for an answer; response can mean obedience or giving what is requested, as rain and plants answer.
THALABI:v2p74/r10.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء الخراساني: يعني فليدعوني للاجابة وفي اللغة الطاعة وإعطاء ما يسأل

THALABI:v2p74/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r11.speaker: كعب بن سعد الغنوي
THALABI:v2p74/r11.claim: Kaʿb ibn Saʿd al-Ghanawi's poem uses istajāba for a supplicant being answered.
THALABI:v2p74/r11.anchor:
وقال كعب بن سعد الغنوي:
وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى

THALABI:v2p74/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r12.speaker: زهير
THALABI:v2p74/r12.claim: Zuhayr's rain poem personifies the earth and rain clouds as asking and answering one another, illustrating response as giving.
THALABI:v2p74/r12.anchor:
وقال زهير
وغيث من الأسمي حق قلاعه

THALABI:v2p74/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p74/r13.claim: The aim is that they be guided.

THALABI:v2p74/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p74/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p74/r14.claim: The author raises the problem that many people supplicate without receiving an apparent answer, despite the promise that God answers the caller; he says scholars differ over the interpretation.
THALABI:v2p74/r14.anchor: ما وجه قوله: أجيب دعوة الداع وقوله ادعوني أستجب لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r1.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says some Companions asked whether their Lord was near so they could speak privately to Him or far so they should call aloud, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك: سأل بعض الصحابة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه؟ فأنزل الله هذه الآية (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's Companions asked where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن سأل أصحاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (¬3) فقالوا: أين ربنا؟ فأنزل الله هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r3.claim: Ata transmits from Ibn Abbas that God's nearness here means being near His friends and people of obedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r3.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: من أوليائي وأهل طاعتي (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r4.claim: The scholars of meaning interpret nearness as God's knowledge, as in 58:7 and 57:4, where He is with people through knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r4.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: يريد قربه بالعلم، كما قال: {ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم} [المجادلة: 7]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses answering a caller's prayer as accepting the worship of one who worships and affirms God's unity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أتقبل عبادة من عبدني ووحدني (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r6.claim: Answering can mean acceptance when prayer means worship: invocations of God's oneness and praise are worship, and acceptance is called response to match the wording.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r6.anchor: ويصح حمل الإجابة على القبول إذا حملت الدعاء على العبادة، والدعاء ضروب، فما كان توحيدا وثناء على الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says ajibu here means I hear: nearness suggests hearing, and response can mean hearing because hearing precedes an answer; not responding may mean not hearing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r7.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: {أجيب} هاهنا معناه: أسمع؛ لأنه أخبر عن قربه تعالى، وظاهر القرب يدل على السماع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r8.claim: The poem about ruins that do not answer when asked uses answering to mean hearing; denying an answer implies denying that the ruins can hear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r8.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
منزلة صم صداها وعفت ... أرسمها إن سئلت لم تجب (¬2) أراد: لم تسمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r9.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r9.claim: The expressions God hears whoever praises Him and the poem about fearing God does not hear me use hearing to mean answering, since hearing and answering follow one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p591/r9.anchor:
وأنشد أحمد بن يحيى عن ابن الأعرابي:
دعوت الله حتى خفت أن لا ... يكون الله يسمع ما أقول (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r1.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says every believer's prayer is answered: it may be granted immediately, stored for the afterlife, or used to avert harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: ما من مؤمن يدعو الله إلا استجاب له، فإما أن عجل له في الدنيا، وإما ادخر (¬2) له في الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r2.claim: Ajibu may be parsed as accusative circumstantial, meaning I am near while answering; its future form is marked nominative by its initial prefix.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r2.anchor: و {أجيب} موضعه نصب (¬4) على الحال، تأويله: فإني قريب مجيبا دعوة الداعي، فلما كان مستقبلا رفع بما في أوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r3.claim: Alternatively, ajibu may start a new clause or attach to qarib as its adjective, meaning near and answering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مستأنفا منقطعا مما قبله، ويجوز أن يكون محمولا على {قريب}. تأويله: فإني قريب مجيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r4.claim: They should answer God through obedience and affirming the messengers; ajaba and istajaba are equivalent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فليستجيبوا لي} أي: فليجيبوني بالطاعة وتصديق الرسل. وأجاب واستجاب بمعنى (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r5.speaker: كعب الغنوي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r5.claim: Kaʿb al-Ghanawi's poem uses istajaba for answering a caller.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r5.anchor:
قال كعب الغنوي (¬7):
وداع دعا يا (¬1) من يجيب إلى الندى ... فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r6.claim: A servant's answer to God is obedience, and each response matches the request: God's command is for obedience, while asking for charity is answered by giving; skies answer with rain and earth with growth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: الإجابة من العبد لله تعالى: الطاعة، وإجابة كل شيء على وفق السؤال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r7.speaker: زهير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r7.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses answered for rain falling upon the hills in response to a rain cloud.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p594/r7.anchor:
قال زهير:
وغيث من الوسمي حو تلاعه ... أجابت روابيه النجاء هواطله (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r1.claim: The phrase means that they may hope to attain right guidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لعلهم يرشدون} أي: ليكونوا على رجاء من إصابة الرشد (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as so that they may be guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لكي يرشدوا (¬1)، ويقال: رشد يرشد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r3.claim: Rashada and rashida mean to attain right guidance, the opposite of error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p595/r3.anchor: ويقال: رشد يرشد ورشد يرشد: إذا أصاب الرشد، وهو نقيض الغي (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says his concise tafsīr aims to lead trained readers from doubt to certain knowledge; beginners lacking adab, grammar, and argument skills will struggle to use it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r1.anchor: هذا بعد أن يكون المتأمل مرتاضا في صنعة الأدب والنحو، مهتديا بطرق الحجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r2.claim: He begins each verse with Ibn ʿAbbās where a transmitted text is available, then other exemplary Companions and Successors, reconciling their statements with the verse wording; he omits interpretations the wording cannot bear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r2.anchor: وأبتدئ في كل آية عند التفسير بقول ابن عباس ما وجدت له نصا (¬5)، ثم بقول من هو قدوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r3.claim: He records the seven readings agreed upon by the regional centers without naming the readers, relying mostly on Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī's book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r3.anchor: وذكرت وجوه القراءات السبع التي اجتمع عليها أهل (¬6) الأمصار، دون تسمية القراء (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r4.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r4.claim: Sahl b. ʿAbd Allāh says even a thousand understandings for every Qurʾānic letter cannot exhaust a verse's meanings, since God's speech has no end and each person understands as God opens the heart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p425/r4.anchor: وهذا سهل بن عبد الله (¬3) يقول: لو أعطي العبد بكل حرف من القرآن ألف فهم

ELMALILI:2:186/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r1.claim: God's nearness means that He promptly answers the person who calls on Him, not that He is near in place or direction.
ELMALILI:2:186/r1.anchor: Demek ki Allah’ın yakınlığının mânası bu vehcile sür‘at-i icâbet demektir; kurb-i mekânî, kurb-i cihet demek değildir.

ELMALILI:2:186/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r2.claim: The verse rebuts naturalists who imagine the Creator as a blind, deaf force and therefore deem prayer and worship useless.
ELMALILI:2:186/r2.anchor: hâlık-ı kâinât olan Hak teâlâ’yı bilmez, işitmez, kör sağır bir kuvvet farz ederek namaz, oruç, dua gibi ibadetleri, müracaatları fâidesiz, lüzumsuz

ELMALILI:2:186/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r3.claim: It also rejects the Ijabiyya, who subject God's knowledge and will to fate and deny divine choice; denying God's creative power or knowledge is sheer ignorance.
ELMALILI:2:186/r3.anchor: mebde’-i kader olan ilm-i ilâhîyi ve mebde’-i kazâ olan irâde-i ilâhiyeyi dahi bir kadere tâbi‘tutarak ihtiyâr-ı ilâhîyi inkâr eden Îcâbiyye’yi şiddetli bir red vardır.

ELMALILI:2:186/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r4.claim: The verse rebukes people who shout and make a commotion in prayer because they imagine God is difficult to hear or far away.
ELMALILI:2:186/r4.anchor: Allah’ı uzak zannedip de dualarında bağıranları red için nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:186/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r5.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
ELMALILI:2:186/r5.claim: In a battle, when the Companions raised their voices in takbir, tahlil, and prayer, the Prophet said they called neither a deaf nor an absent being, but One who hears and is near.
ELMALILI:2:186/r5.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz “Siz, sağıra veya gāibe dua etmiyorsunuz, her hâlde bir semî‘-i karîbe dua ediyorsunuz” buyurmuştu.

ELMALILI:2:186/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r6.claim: One condition of prayer is humility and reverent concentration; God is nearer than the jugular vein and closer to people than they are to themselves.
ELMALILI:2:186/r6.anchor: Bunun için duanın şerâitinden biri de hudû‘ve huşû‘dur. Zira insanlar Allah’tan uzak olsalar da “Allah karîb”dir, bize şah damarımızdan daha karîbdir

ELMALILI:2:186/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r7.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:2:186/r7.claim: Razi argues that a possible thing receives existence only through its Maker, who stands between its essence and existence and is nearer to that essence than its existence is.
ELMALILI:2:186/r7.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “İşbu فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ kavl-i ilâhîsinde bir sırr-ı aklî vardır. Şöyle ki, mâhiyyât-i mümkinâtın vücudlarıyla ittisâfı ancak îcâd-ı Sâni‘iledir.

ELMALILI:2:186/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r8.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:2:186/r8.claim: Razi's higher argument says God causes not only possible essences to exist but each quiddity to be what it is, making Him nearer to every essence than it is to itself.
ELMALILI:2:186/r8.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “İşbu فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ kavl-i ilâhîsinde bir sırr-ı aklî vardır.

ELMALILI:2:186/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r9.claim: Elmalılı says Razi's first argument treats essences as uncreated and the second as created; philosophers and Sufis accept the former, theologians the latter, with different conceptual priority between knowledge and will.
ELMALILI:2:186/r9.anchor: Râzî’nin birinci takrîri mâhiyyâtın gayr-i mec‘ûl olmasına, ikinci takrîri de mec‘ûl olmasına göredir

ELMALILI:2:186/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r10.claim: God is the source of every necessity: possible existence derives from Necessary Existence, as do universal matters and possible essences; without God there is neither existence nor logic.
ELMALILI:2:186/r10.anchor: Vücûdât-ı mümkine vücûd-ı vâcibden müstefâd olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:2:186/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r11.claim: Treating possible essences as eternally uncreated would multiply self-necessary principles or posit a principle binding God, contradicting God's sole status as First Cause.
ELMALILI:2:186/r11.anchor: Böyle bir iddia bizâtihi ve lizâtihi mebâdî-i zarûriyenin, lizâtihi vâcibü’l-vücûdun ta‘addüdüne kāil olmaktır. Hâlbuki bizâtihi ve lizâtihi illetü’l-‘ilel birdir, o da Allah teâlâ’dır.

ELMALILI:2:186/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r12.claim: Even the necessary judgment that a thing is itself ultimately depends on considering God's necessary existence; all truth-assent depends on affirming the Necessary Being.
ELMALILI:2:186/r12.anchor: Bu suretle her nefsü’l-emr tasdîki, tasdîk-i vâcibe mütevakkıftır. Binâen‘aleyh bütün vücûbların, zarûretlerin menşe’i Cenâb-ı Hak’tır.

ELMALILI:2:186/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r13.claim: Since people hear and answer one another's hopes and requests, they must believe that God, nearer to them than they are to themselves, hears their prayers even sooner.
ELMALILI:2:186/r13.anchor: biz kendimizin ve başkalarının recâ ve temenniyâtını duyup bilebiliyor ve onlara işittiğimiz zaman cevap da verebiliyorsak, bize bizden daha yakın olan Allah teâlâ’nın dualarımızı

ELMALILI:2:186/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r14.claim: Duʿāʾ is originally a verbal noun meaning calling, like daʿwat; conventionally it means a subordinate's request or entreaty to a superior and is also used as a noun.
ELMALILI:2:186/r14.anchor: “Duâ”, esasen “da‘vet” gibi çağırmak mânasına masdardır. Sonra küçükten büyüğe, aşağıdan yukarıya vâki‘olan taleb ü niyaz mânasına örf olmuş

ELMALILI:2:186/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r15.claim: The reality of prayer is the servant's seeking help, care, and assistance from the Lord.
ELMALILI:2:186/r15.anchor: Duanın hakikati, kulun Rabbi celle celâluhu’dan istimdad ve inâyet ü me‘ûnet istid‘â etmesidir.

ELMALILI:2:186/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r16.claim: Elmalılı rejects as ignorant the claim that prayer is useless, especially among advocates of a blind natural force and adherents of necessitarian or compulsion theories.
ELMALILI:2:186/r16.anchor: İlimden dem vuran bazı câhiller duâyı fâidesiz bir şey zannetmişlerdir. Bunların başında kudret-i fâtırayı bir kuvvet-i ‘amyâ zu‘m eden kör kuvvetçiler vardır.

ELMALILI:2:186/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r17.speaker: Îcâb veya cebir nazariyelerine saplananlar
ELMALILI:2:186/r17.claim: The objectors argue that a request already known by God to occur must occur necessarily, while one not known to occur is impossible, so prayer is needless either way.
ELMALILI:2:186/r17.anchor: Bunlardan başka îcab veya cebir nazariyelerine saplananlardan da bu babda birtakım şüpheler îrâdına kalkışanlar olmuştur. Şöyle ki: 1. Dua ile matlub

ELMALILI:2:186/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r18.claim: The second fatalist objection says events are fixed by an eternal cause: what it decreed is necessary, what it did not decree impossible, so prayer can neither increase nor decrease destiny.
ELMALILI:2:186/r18.anchor: Bu âlemdeki bütün hâdisâtın bir müessir-i kadîme müntehî olduğunda şüphe yoktur. O hâlde bu müessir-i kadîmin ezelde vücûdunu iktizâ ettiği şey

ELMALILI:2:186/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r19.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz
ELMALILI:2:186/r19.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying God determined destinies a certain number of years before creating creation; Elmalılı gives no grading.
ELMALILI:2:186/r19.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz bile “قَدَّرَ اللّٰهُّٰ الْمَقَادِيرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْلُقَ الْخَلْقَ بِكَذَا وَكَذَا عَامًا: Allah mekādîri, halkı halk etmezden

ELMALILI:2:186/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r20.claim: Elmalılı also cites the saying that the pen has dried concerning what will be.
ELMALILI:2:186/r20.anchor: kezâlik جَفَّ الْقَلَمُ بِمَا هُوَ كَائِنٌ buyurmamış mıdır?

ELMALILI:2:186/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r21.claim: He cites a hadith that four matters are already finished: lifespan, provision, creation, and character; no grading is given.
ELMALILI:2:186/r21.anchor: Dört şeyden ferâgat hâsıl olmuştur: Ömür, rızık, halk, ahlâk

ELMALILI:2:186/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r22.claim: Just as God answers their prayers, people must answer His call and believe in Him.
ELMALILI:2:186/r22.anchor: O hâlde onlar da Benim davetime koşsunlar ve Bana hakkıyla iman etsinler

ELMALILI:2:186/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186/r23.claim: Responding to God and believing in Him enables people to proceed in right guidance.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r1.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r1.claim: Some object that predestination makes supplication futile: what is decreed will occur, while what is not decreed will not occur.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r1.anchor: duayı terk etmek evlâ olduğu bu vücûh ile sâbit olmaz mı? demeye kadar varanlar olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r2.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r2.claim: They argue that God already knows hidden intentions and circumstances, so prayer cannot inform Him and seems unnecessary.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r2.anchor: Hak sübhânehu allâmü’l-guyûbdur. Gözlerin hâin bakışını, sînelerin gizli tuttuğu niyetleri bilir.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r3.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r3.claim: Some cite Gabriel’s and Abraham’s surrendering sayings, acceptance of divine decree, and a sacred hadith preferring remembrance to asking to argue that leaving supplication is better.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r3.anchor: duayı terk etmek evlâ olduğu bu vücûh ile sâbit olmaz mı? demeye kadar varanlar olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r4.claim: The overwhelming majority of rational people and scholars affirm that supplication is among the most important stations of servitude, supported by many rational and transmitted proofs.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r4.anchor: ukalâ ve ulemânın cumhûr-ı a‘zamı duanın ehemm-i makāmât-ı ubûdiyet olduğunda tereddüd etmemişlerdir

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r5.claim: The predestination objection is incomplete: some outcomes are decreed conditional on supplication, just as satiety depends on eating and success on seeking and effort.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r5.anchor: Taleb ile, dua ile mukayyed olarak ma‘lûmü’l-vukū‘olan mukadderât vardır.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r6.claim: Created beings, not God, are subject to decree; prayer acknowledges divine precedence and is therefore a high form of worship.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r6.anchor: kadere mahkum olan Allah değil mahlûkāttır. Kaderler sâbık ise Cenâb-ı Allah da kazâ ve kadere sâbık

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r7.claim: Because the secret of decree is unknown before it occurs, divine wisdom requires people to act between hope, which motivates success, and caution, which orders it; human duties remain valid.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r8.claim: Since events are tied to causes and effort follows laws, supplication is itself one of the causes through which decreed outcomes occur.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r9.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r9.claim: Companions asked whether deeds were already settled or newly determined; the Prophet answered that they were settled, then commanded them to act because each person is eased toward what they were created for.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r9.anchor: Ashâb-ı kirâm Resûlullah’a cebr ü kader meselesini sormuşlar: “Yâ Resûlullah nasıl görürsün?

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r10.claim: The prophetic answer preserves a middle position: neither absolute compulsion nor unrestricted freedom, but a balance of divine determination and human choice, with people facilitated rather than coerced.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r11.claim: Supplication aims to display servitude and return in humility and abasement, not to inform God.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r11.anchor: Duadan maksud i‘lâm değil, izhâr-ı ubûdiyet, arz-ı zillet ü inkisar ile müracaattır.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r12.claim: Praying while accepting divine decree does not put human preference ahead of God; it magnifies divine power above all else.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r12.anchor: kazâ ve kaderine rızâ ile beraber Allah’a dua etmek

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r13.claim: The sayings attributed to Gabriel and Abraham are, fitting their station, eloquent forms of prayer; silent state can speak more eloquently than words for a sincere person in God’s presence.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r14.claim: A prayer need not state a request explicitly; direct speech, allusion, or an inwardly expressive state can each constitute supplication.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r14.anchor: Daha doğrusu dua sarih olduğu gibi kinaye ve îmâ ile de olur.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r15.claim: Because praise to the Generous also contains supplication, a hadith calls praise of God the best supplication.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r15.anchor: bu sebeple أَفْضَلُ الدُّعَاءِ اَلْحَمْدُ للّٰهِّٰ buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r16.claim: Many Qur’anic passages command or commend supplication; the warning about hardened hearts shows that God is angry with those who do not turn to Him.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r16.anchor: Sonuncusu gösteriyor ki Allah istemeyenlere gazab eder.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r17.claim: Al-Fatiha had already been described as the Sura of Supplication and Teaching the Request, and as instruction in the etiquette of prayer.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r17.anchor: Sûre-i Fâtiha’nın “Sûre-i Duâ” ve “Ta‘lîm-i Mes’ele” isimlerini de hâiz olduğu

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r18.claim: The Qur’an gives fourteen question-and-answer passages, on foundational and practical matters; most use qul or faqul, with the prefixed fa signaling an immediate answer and delivery.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r18.anchor: Ekserîsinde قُلْ yerinde فَقُلْ buyurulmuştur ki, bu فا’da cevâbın müsta‘celiyetine

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r19.claim: Unlike the other answers, God replies directly without saying qul or faqul, omitting the intermediary and expressing nearness through His promise to answer prayer.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r19.anchor: cevâbında doğrudan doğru فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ buyurulmuş, vâsıta hazf edilmiş

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r20.claim: God says “I am near,” rather than “My servants are near Me,” because a contingent creature cannot approach God by its own being; nearness comes from God’s side.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r20.anchor: kurbiyet taraf-ı abdden değil, taraf-ı Hak’dandır.

ELMALILI:2:186#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r21.claim: A person occupied with anything besides God has not truly prayed; when absorbed in knowledge of the One and relinquishing personal claims, all intermediaries fall away and divine nearness is realized.
ELMALILI:2:186#2/r21.anchor: dua eden kimsenin gönlü Allah’ın gayrısıyla meşgul olduğu müddetçe hakikaten dua etmiş olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r1.claim: When the worshipper stops attending to personal interests and relinquishes all intermediaries, divine nearness becomes possible; surrender to God is fully realized.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r1.anchor: kendi hakkını mülâhaza ve nasîb-i beşeriyeti talepten imtinâ‘eder, vesâit bi’l-külliye mürtefi‘olur

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r2.claim: When self-interest is removed, surrender expressed in “I entrust my affair to God” appears fully; perception and desire become God-oriented, and divine will brings about what countless causes and centuries could not.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r2.anchor: milyonlarca esbâbın, asırlarca zamanların yapamadığı şeyler

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r3.claim: A prophetic hadith calls supplication the marrow of worship, supporting the author’s view that it is a means of nearness and among the best acts of worship.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r3.anchor: اَلدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ: dua ibadetin iliğidir

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r4.claim: Another hadith defines worship as supplication and cites the command to call upon God and receive His response.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r4.anchor: اَلدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ: ibadet duadan ibarettir” diyerek ٱدْعُونِىٓ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ âyetini okumuştur.

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r5.claim: Those who belittle supplication also belittle worship, fail to know God as near and responsive, and instead value the attention of creatures or take them as rivals.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r5.anchor: Dikkat edilirse görülür ki duayı mühimsemeyenler

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r6.claim: After the fasting commands, God reassures the Messenger that He is near and answers those who call; this directs attention to supplication, especially in the state of fasting.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r6.anchor: İşte Cenâb-ı Allah bu babdaki bütün şüpheleri def‘ve ‘ibâdını irşad için duanın ehemmiyetine

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r7.claim: The servants’ response should be wholehearted obedience to God’s commands; they should also believe Him and affirm what He has taught about fasting’s virtues, so that they may attain right guidance and their aims.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r7.anchor: onlar da Benim emirlerime candan icâbet ü imtisal etsinler

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r8.claim: Supplication and command are requests in the same grammatical form: a needy person’s cry for help is a prayer, while the helper’s “get up” is a response and command.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r8.anchor: Mâlumdur ki dua ile emir, aynı sîga ile yapılan birer talebdirler.

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r9.claim: The greater’s aid to the distressed is a mark of greatness; obedience to the greater is also required by good manners, reason, and the subjects’ own benefit, and rational action is called rushd.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r9.anchor: Muktezâ-yı akıl üzere harekete ise “rüşd” tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r10.claim: God is the absolute Greatest, present everywhere, able to meet every need, and nearer to people than they are to themselves; He explicitly promises to answer prayer.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r10.anchor: her yerde hâzır u nâzır, mahlûkātının her türlü hâcetlerini is‘âfa kādir ve onlara kendilerinden daha karîb

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r11.claim: The verse establishes that those who believe in God and His rulings and obey them demonstrate sound reason and guidance, enabling them to reach their aims.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r11.anchor: ancak Allah’a ve ahkâmına îmân ile icâbet ü itâ‘at edenlerdir ki akl ü rüşdlerini isbât etmiş olur

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r12.claim: The verse supports the implementation of the fasting rulings and, by extension, all divine commands; fasting receives special emphasis because it seems especially difficult and contrary to appetite.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r12.anchor: Bu tevsîk ıtlâkıyla bütün evâmir ü ahkâma şâmil ise de bilhassa emr-i sıyâmı tâkip etmesi şâyân-ı dikkattir.

ELMALILI:2:186#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r13.claim: Elmalılı postpones the remaining details about supplication and returns to the discussion of fasting.
ELMALILI:2:186#3/r13.anchor: O hâlde dua hakkındaki diğer tafsîlâtı gelecek olan diğer âyetlere bırakarak oruca devam edelim.

QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r10.claim: The question reveals the questioners’ spiritual state: they asked about God Himself, not a legal ruling, creature, religion, worldly matter, or afterlife.
QUSHAYRI:v1p88/r10.anchor: لم يسألوا عن حكم ولا عن مخلوق

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r1.claim: These servants differ from those asking Muhammad about mountains, orphans, menstruation, the Spirit, wine and gambling, or fighting in the sacred month.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r1.anchor: وليس هؤلاء من جملة من قال

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r2.claim: Although Muhammad is the messenger between God and creation, God takes over the answer rather than speaking through the Prophet’s tongue.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r2.anchor: فأنت وإن كنت السفير بيننا وبين الخلق

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r3.claim: God’s direct first-person answer removes intermediaries from the language of nearness; He says “I am near,” not “tell them I am near.”
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r3.anchor: رفع الواسطة من الأغيار عن القربة

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r4.claim: Divine nearness is not directional or tied to a place: God is exalted above spatial approach, distance, and location.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r4.anchor: تقدس الحق سبحانه عن كل اقتراب بجهة

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r5.claim: God is near all through knowledge, power, hearing, and sight, and especially near believers through care, victory, and answered prayer, never by essence or place.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r5.anchor: وهو قريب من المؤمنين على وجه التبرية والنصرة

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r6.claim: God promises to answer a caller whenever, however, and wherever the caller invokes Him, without requiring a prior claim of ascetic merit or a particular worship-time.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r6.anchor: لم يعد إجابة من كان باستحقاق زهد أو في زمان عبادة

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r7.claim: “Let them respond to Me” is a duty, while “I answer the caller” is reassurance and ease; God puts the reassurance before the obligation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r7.anchor: تعريف وتخفيف ، قدم التخفيف على التكليف

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r8.claim: God’s answer invites the servant’s prayer, and the servant should answer God’s call; divine generosity is not compelled by the servant’s invocation.

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r9.claim: Believing in God here means trusting Him, since He answers whoever calls Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r9.anchor: وليثقوا في ، فإني أجيب من دعاني

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r10.speaker: قائلهم
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r10.claim: An anonymous poem swears allegiance to the beloved and refuses any substitute, affirming trust in the beloved alone.
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r10.anchor: قال قائلهم : يا عز أقسم بالذي أنا عبده

QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r11.claim: The purpose of the command and the servant’s prayer is that the servant arrive at guidance.
