QUSHAYRI:v1p89/r11.anchor: أي ليس القصد من تكليفك ودعائك إلا وصولك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r1.claim: The verse’s placement after the command to magnify God addresses how finite, frail people can relate to a supremely great Lord and opens a path to conscious worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyetin sonlarında Allah’ın eşsiz ve benzersiz büyüklüğü, ululuğu hatırlatılıp kulların da bunu dile getirmeleri istenmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r2.claim: God is near to His servants, present at every time and place; transcendent greatness does not require spatial distance. The author links this nearness to 56:85, 50:16, and 8:24.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r2.anchor: Âyet, o keyfiyetsiz ve akıl almaz büyüklüğün sahibi bulunan rabbin kullarına yakın olduğunu, her an ve her yerde hazır ve nâzır bulunduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r3.claim: Bodily pleasures such as eating, drinking, and sex can keep people from consciously experiencing closeness to God and attending to realities beyond the physical world.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r3.anchor: Kulun Allah’a yakınlığını şuur halinde yaşaması ve hissetmesine mani olan şeyler arasında yeme, içme, cinsel ilişki gibi beden zevkleri de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r4.claim: Fasting temporarily closes the windows to bodily pleasure and offers a chance to experience God’s nearness and presence more consciously than on days of eating and drinking.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r4.anchor: Belli bir süre bedenî zevklere açılan pencereleri kapatan oruç, diğerlerinin açılması için insana önemli bir fırsat sunmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r5.claim: Right guidance in relations with people, the world, and God requires knowing God and relating to Him through worship and awareness of worship; this is a condition of fully realized humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r5.anchor: Kâmil insanlığın şartı Allah’ı tanımak, O’nunla ibadet yoluyla ve ibadet şuuruyla ilişki kurmaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r6.claim: The verse describes worship as joining God’s call and accepting His invitation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r6.anchor: Âyet bunu “Allah’ın çağrısına katılmak, davetini kabul etmek” şeklinde ifade ediyor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r7.claim: Prayer is one form of worship; the closest, warmest relation with God is formed in prostration and in sincere supplication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r7.anchor: Kulun rabbi ile en yakın ve sıcak ilişkisi namazda secde halinde ve içten gelerek yapılan dua ve niyaz halinde kurulan ilişkidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r8.claim: Answering God’s call yields awareness of His nearness, the ability to think and act rightly, and the granting of one’s supplication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r8.anchor: Allah’ın çağrısına kulak veren, O’nun dinine giren bir kimse bundan üç önemli kazanç elde etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r9.claim: A cited hadith says each person’s prayer is answered unless they grow impatient and complain that it was not answered.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r9.anchor: Acele etmedikçe her birinizin duası kabul edilir. Bu sebeple (acelecilik yüzünden) insan, dua ettim de kabul olunmadı der

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r10.claim: A second cited hadith says a supplicant receives one of three outcomes: the request now, its postponement for their benefit, or expiation of a sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r10.anchor: Ya istediği hemen verilir ya lehine ertelenip saklanır yahut da dua bir günahına kefâret olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r11.claim: The author poses the apparent problem that if destiny determines all events and requests absent from one’s destiny will not be granted, supplication seems useless.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r11.anchor: Kader inancına göre olacak ve olmayacak her şey bellidir, kulun istedikleri de kaderinde yoksa kendisine verilmeyecektir. Şu halde duanın faydası nedir?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r12.claim: God orders events in the material world through laws and causes, using intermediaries such as parents for birth, clouds for rain, causes for death, and organs for hearing and sight.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r12.anchor: Allah Teâlâ madde âleminde olup bitenleri kanunlara ve sebeplere bağlamıştır. İnsanı bir ana ve babadan (onları aracı kılarak) yaratmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r13.claim: Seeking God without means is like asking for birth without parents or sight without eyes; relying only on means while forgetting God is equally mistaken. Islam calls for using means while turning to God, who controls causes and outcomes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r13.anchor: İslâm’ın gösterdiği yol hem sebepleri ve aracıları kullanmak, ihmal etmemek hem de sebep ve sonuç elinde olan, bunlara hâkim bulunan Allah’a yönelmektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r14.claim: Giving, withholding, and supplication all belong to destiny; asking does not oppose destiny but occurs within it. People should understand destiny as what will happen, not as a demand that events be otherwise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r14.anchor: Allah’ın vermesi ve vermemesi kadere bağlı olduğu gibi dua da kadere bağlıdır. Kul ister Allah verir. İstemek kadere aykırı değildir, kader çerçevesi içindedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r15.claim: The author concludes that God will answer a servant who supplicates with proper etiquette.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:186/r15.anchor: Kul âdâbına uygun şekilde dua ederse Allah da kabul edecektir.

BAQILLANI:v1p250/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r1.claim: He rejects explaining the first generation’s inability only through reports of unseen events: that concedes the central claim that Qur’anic composition is inimitable.
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r1.anchor: بأنهم لا يقدرون على معارضته في الإخبار عن الغيوب إن قدروا على مثل نظمه

BAQILLANI:v1p250/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r2.claim: Later generations are even less able to match the Qur’an, since the first Arabs’ varied eloquence was unsurpassed and later speakers could at best equal it.
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r2.anchor: فصاحة أولئك في وجوه ما كانوا يتفننون فيه من القول مما لا يزيد عليه فصاحة من بعدهم

BAQILLANI:v1p250/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r3.claim: The same method establishes incapacity in every age: the challenge, human competitiveness, and obligation are constant; he cites the challenge to all humans and jinn.
BAQILLANI:v1p250/r3.anchor: التحدي في الكل على جهة واحدة والتنافس في الطباع على حد واحد والتكليف على منهاج لا يختلف

BURHAN:v4p52/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p52/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v4p52/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no community asked fewer questions than Muḥammad’s community: its fourteen questions received answers, including this question and the listed questions in al-Baqara and other sūras.
BURHAN:v4p52/r1.anchor: نقل عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال ما كان قوم اقل سؤالا

BURHAN:v4p52/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p52/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p52/r2.claim: The questions are arranged around two themes: asking about God’s essence and attribute in al-Baqara, then about the afterlife through questions about the mountains and the Hour.
BURHAN:v4p52/r2.anchor: ولهذه المسألة ترتيب اثنان منها في شرح المبدأ

BURHAN:v4p52/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p52/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p52/r5.claim: Al-Zarkashī raises why this answer begins directly with God’s nearness instead of the usual قل, as in the answer about the new moons; this excerpt leaves the question open.
BURHAN:v4p52/r5.anchor: وعادة السؤال يجيء جوابه في القرآن بقل نحو

BURHAN:v1p46/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p46/r1.claim: The fragment says رأيت takes a direct object because it contains the sense of تنظر.
BURHAN:v1p46/r1.anchor: فإن قلت من أين جاءت إلى ورأيت يتعدى بنفسه أجيب لتضمنه معنى تنظر

BURHAN:v1p398/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p398/r1.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p398/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās distinguishes yāʾs omitted from the written text but retained in recitation from yāʾs omitted in both, then divides the first kind into pronoun and root-letter yāʾ.
BURHAN:v1p398/r1.anchor: قال أبو العباس الياء الناقصة في الخط ضربان ضرب محذوف في الخط ثابت في التلاوة

BURHAN:v1p398/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p398/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p398/r4.claim: The written omission of the object pronoun in دعان signals a prayer arising from the unseen realm with inward sincerity.
BURHAN:v1p398/r4.anchor: فحذف الضمير في الخط دلالة على الدعاء الذي من جهة الملكوت

BURHAN:v1p400/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p400/r9.speaker: أبو العباس
BURHAN:v1p400/r9.claim: When the omitted yāʾ is a word’s root ending, as in الداع, it signals a petitioner whose heart and ultimate aim are devoted to God in the unseen and afterlife rather than the present world.
BURHAN:v1p400/r9.anchor: والقسم الثاني من الضرب الأول إذا كانت الياء لام الكلمة سواء كانت في الاسم

BURHAN:v2p16/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p16/r2.claim: The promise to answer prayer, like ادعوني أستجب لكم, is qualified by God’s will, a qualification explained in the following discussion.
BURHAN:v2p16/r2.anchor: ﴿ أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان ﴾ وقوله ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ 7 فإنه معلق

BURHAN:v2p16/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p16/r3.claim: Usulists disagree whether applying an unrestricted text to a restricted one follows Arabic usage or analogy; proponents of the linguistic view cite Arabs’ preference for brevity and omission, as in عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد.
BURHAN:v2p16/r3.anchor: اختلف الأصوليون في أن حمل المطلق على المقيد هل هو من وضع اللغة

BURHAN:v2p16/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r4.speaker: إمام الحرمين
BURHAN:v2p16/r4.claim: Imām al-Ḥaramayn rejects the claim that the Qurʾān is like one verse, allowing unrestricted wording to be restricted elsewhere: only the eternal divine attribute is one, while its expressions are multiple and include opposites.
BURHAN:v2p16/r4.anchor: قال إمام الحرمين وهذا غلط لأن الموصوف بالاتحاد الصفة القديمة المختصة بالذات

BURHAN:v2p16/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p16/r5.claim: When unrestricted and restricted rulings concern the same subject, conflicting specifications—continuous fasting, broken fasting, or days left open—mean the original unrestricted wording remains unrestricted.
BURHAN:v2p16/r5.anchor: والثاني كإطلاق صوم الأيام في كفارة اليمين وقيدت بالتتابع في كفارة الظهار

BURHAN:v2p16/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p16/r6.claim: Silence in a different ruling does not transfer a restriction: tayammum’s two limbs do not inherit ablution’s four, and a food option in one expiation cannot be imported into another.
BURHAN:v2p16/r6.anchor: فأما إذا حكم في شيء بأمور لم يحكم في شيء آخر ينقض تلك الأمور

BURHAN:v2p188/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p188/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p188/r8.claim: Apparent nonresponse is qualified by the verse saying God uncovers what people call for if He wills; the Prophet explains that a sinless, non-estranging supplication is answered immediately, saved for the afterlife, or matched by averting harm.
BURHAN:v2p188/r8.anchor: وكثير من الناس يدعون فلا يستجاب لهم وبيانه بقوله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p367/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p367/r1.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v2p367/r1.claim: When a conditional clause introduced by wāw is circumstantial, it needs no apodosis: the clause functions like a dependent adverbial, normally a single constituent, rather than an independent sentence.
BURHAN:v2p367/r1.anchor: قال ابن جني وإنما كان كذلك لأن الحال فضلة وأصل وضع الفضلة

BURHAN:v2p367/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p367/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p367/r2.claim: If the conditional clause receives its own answer, the wāw is coordinative rather than circumstantial; otherwise the sentence would lack an apodosis.
BURHAN:v2p367/r2.anchor: فإن أجيب الشرط كانت الواو عاطفة لا للحال نحو أحسن إليه

BURHAN:v2p509/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p509/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v2p509/r1.claim: Ibn Mālik objects to Ibn al-Ḥājib’s use of الرحمن as an example of a noun ending in added alif and nūn: it is a divine proper name, normally inseparable from the article and rarely bare except in vocative.
BURHAN:v2p509/r1.anchor: أنكر ابن مالك على ابن الحاجب تمثيله ب الرحمن

BURHAN:v2p509/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p509/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p509/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, unaware of Ibn Mālik’s argument, dismissed it as stubbornness in disbelief; al-Shāṭibī’s line using رحمانا was criticized for intending the established divine name.
BURHAN:v2p509/r2.anchor: ولم يحضر الزمخشري هذا الجواب فذكر أنه من تعنتهم في كفرهم

BURHAN:v2p509/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p509/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p509/r7.claim: The pattern فعّال also expresses intensive meanings, as in غفّار, منّان, توّاب, وهّاب, فعّال لما يريد, and صبّار شكور.
BURHAN:v2p509/r7.anchor: وأما فعال فنحو غفار ومنان وتواب

BURHAN:v4p42/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p42/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p42/r1.claim: An answer normally matches its question, but may redirect the hearer to the important issue, be broader to meet an overlooked need, or be narrower as circumstances require; al-Sakkākī calls redirection أسلوب الحكيم.
BURHAN:v4p42/r1.anchor: الأصل في الجواب إن يكون مطابقا

BURHAN:v4p348/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p348/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p348/r7.claim: A lām can follow an apparent an without carrying causation when the speech contains the sense of intent or will.
BURHAN:v4p348/r7.anchor: وقد تقع موقع أن وإن كانت غير معلولة لها في المعنى وذلك إن كان الكلام متضمنا لمعنى القصد والإرادة

BURHAN:v4p348/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p348/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p348/r9.claim: The jussive lām is a lām of command, marking that the speaker requests an action; it normally governs a verb whose subject is not the addressee.
BURHAN:v4p348/r9.anchor: الثالث الجازمة وهى الموضوعة للطلب وتسمى لام الأمر وتدخل على المضارع لتؤذن أنه مطلوب للمتكلم وشرطها أن يكون الفعل لغير المخاطب

BURHAN:v4p348/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p348/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p348/r11.claim: The command lām is kasra when it begins a clause and is silent after wāw or fāʾ, as in this verse’s two commands.

BURHAN:v1p93/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p93/r1.claim: The closing phrase after the command to pray and expect a response is an unmatched Qur’anic ending; this verse follows the command to fast and honor Ramadan.
BURHAN:v1p93/r1.anchor: قد تكون الفاصلة لا نظير لها فى القرآن

BURHAN:v1p93/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p93/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p93/r2.claim: Some read the ending as an allusion to Laylat al-Qadr: people need guidance to recognize it, and it is among the most hoped-for times for answered prayer.
BURHAN:v1p93/r2.anchor: وقيل فيه تعريض بليلة القدر أى لعلهم يرشدون إلى معرفتها وإنما يحتاجون للإرشاد إلى ما لا يعلمون

SULAMI:v1p71/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p71/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p71/r1.claim: Sahl calls modesty before God the lowest station of spiritual nearness.
SULAMI:v1p71/r1.anchor: قال سهل : أدنى مقامات القرب الحياء من الله عز وجل

ITQAN:v1p284/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r1.speaker: جابر
ITQAN:v1p284/r1.claim: A very weak report says that after reciting this verse the Prophet prayed at length, affirming that God commanded supplication and guaranteed its answer.
ITQAN:v1p284/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه والديلمي وابن أبي الدنيا في الدعاء وغيرهم بسند ضعيف جدا عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ ﴿ وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب ﴾ الآية فقال اللهم أمرت بالدعاء وتكفلت بالإجابة

ITQAN:v2p577/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p577/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p577/r1.claim: Al-Bazzar reports Ibn Abbas saying the Companions asked the Prophet only twelve questions, all answered in the Qur'an; al-Razi gives fourteen question forms, eight in al-Baqara, including these examples.
ITQAN:v2p577/r1.anchor: أخرج البزار عن ابن عباس قال ما رأيت قوما خيرا من أصحاب محمد ما سألوه إلا عن اثنتي عشرة مسألة كلها في القرآن

ITQAN:v2p577/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p577/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p577/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti corrects the count: the questions about the spirit and Dhul-Qarnayn came from Meccan polytheists and Jews, not Companions, leaving twelve Companion questions as in the sound report.
ITQAN:v2p577/r2.anchor: قلت السائل عن الروح وعن ذي القرنين مشركو مكة واليهود كما في أسباب النزول لا الصحابة فالخالص اثنا عشر

ITQAN:v3p303/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p303/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p303/r1.claim: The expected قل is omitted from the answer because a servant at prayer occupies the noblest station, with no intermediary between the servant and the Master.
ITQAN:v3p303/r1.anchor: فإن قيل كيف جاء ﴿ وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب ﴾ وعادة السؤال يجئ جوابه في القرآن ( بقل ) قلنا حذفت للإشارة

ITQAN:v3p276#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r1.claim: The endings after the command to lower the gaze and after the command to supplicate and respond are distinctive Quranic fawasil without a parallel.
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r1.anchor: في الفواصل ما لا نظير له في القرآن كقوله عقب الأمر بالغض في سورة النور ﴿ إن الله خبير بما يصنعون ﴾ وقوله عقب الأمر بالدعاء والاستجابة ﴿ لعلهم يرشدون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p276#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r2.claim: Another view takes the closing phrase as an allusion to Laylat al-Qadr: after mentioning Ramadan, it says they may be guided to recognize the Night.
ITQAN:v3p276#2/r2.anchor: وقيل فيه تعريض بليلة القدر حيث ذكر ذلك عقب ذكر رمضان أي لعلهم يرشدون إلى معرفتها

ITQAN:v3p19/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.claim: The divine nearness in both verses is interpreted as nearness by knowledge.
ITQAN:v3p19/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك صفة القرب في قوله ﴿ فإني قريب ﴾ ﴿ ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد ﴾ أي بالعلم

ITQAN:v3p19/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r11.claim: The Quran’s many references to mercy are listed among the divine attributes discussed in this section.

ITQAN:v3p19/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.claim: The general rule is that an attribute whose literal reality is impossible for God is interpreted through its necessary implication.
ITQAN:v3p19/r12.anchor: وقد قال العلماء كل صفة يستحيل حقيقتها على الله تعالى تفسر بلازمها

ITQAN:v3p19/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi says psychological states have an onset and an outcome: divine anger means intending harm, not bodily agitation, and divine shyness means refraining, not inward shrinking.
ITQAN:v3p19/r13.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين جميع الأعراض النفسانية أعني الرحمة والفرح والسرور والغضب والحياء والمكر والاستهزاء لها أوائل ولها غايات

TUSTARI:2:186/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:186/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:186/r1.claim: Responding to God means supplicating; believing Him means affirming Him, for He is present when sincerely called without despair or loss of hope.
TUSTARI:2:186/r1.anchor: أي يصدقوني، فأنا حيث ما دعاني مخلصا لا آيسا ولا قنطا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r1.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r1.claim: A Bedouin asked whether God was near, so they could converse privately, or far, so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r1.anchor: عن الصلت بن حكيم بن معاوية بن حيدة عن أبيه عن جدة قال جاء أعرابي إلى النبي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r2.speaker: الحسن
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet’s Companions asked where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed; al-Suyuti notes the report is mursal and has other routes.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال سأل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا فأنزل الله

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r3.speaker: علي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r3.claim: Ali reports that after the Prophet urged people not to tire of supplication, a man asked whether God hears prayer; the verse was then revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r3.anchor: عن علي قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تعجزوا عن الدعاء فإن الله أنزل علي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r4.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r4.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says people wondered when to pray after 40:60 (“Call upon Me; I will answer you”), so 2:186 through “they may be rightly guided” was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p33/r4.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح أنه بلغه لما نزلت ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p374/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r2.claim: Qarīb means responsive: God is near in the sense of answering those who call upon Him.
DAMGHANI:v1p374/r2.anchor: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فاني قريب أجيب دعوة الداعي إذا دعان أي مجيب لهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r1.claim: The fifth sense of du'a is asking or supplication, as in God's answering the caller, Moses being asked to pray for relief, and the condemned asking Hell's keepers to pray for them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r1.anchor: والخامس : السؤال . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r2.claim: The sixth sense is questioning: asking Moses to clarify what the cow is, or asking the false gods whether they are deities.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r2.anchor: والسادس : الاستفهام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p294/r3.claim: The seventh sense is punishment: the fire calls and torments those who turned away.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r1.claim: Qurb ordinarily means nearness in distance, the opposite of remoteness; qurban can be an offering to God or a king's close associates.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r1.anchor: الأصل في القرب : أنه الدنو من المسافة . وضده : البعد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r2.claim: The verb 'aqrabat is used of a sheep nearing delivery, but not of a she-camel.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r2.anchor: واقربت الشاة دنا نتاجها . لا يقال : للناقة : اقربت .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit describes a garment as muqarib and says this label is not used when it is not good.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : ثوب مقارب ، ولا يقال مقارب إذا لم يكن جيدا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r4.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r4.claim: Another linguist says a garment called muqarib with kasra is poor, while with fatha it is inexpensive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r4.anchor: وقال غيره : ثوب مقارب - بكسر الراء - ليس بجيد - وبفتحها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r5.claim: A qarib is a small boat traveling with larger sea ships for quick errands; the word also means a person seeking water at night.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r5.anchor: والقارب : سفينة صغيرة تكون مع أصحاب السفن البحرية

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r6.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r6.claim: Ibn Faris transmits that some linguists restrict qarib, the water-seeker, to someone who seeks water at night rather than by day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r6.anchor: وحكى ابن فارس عن بعض اللغويين : أنه لا يقال ذلك لطالب الماء نهارا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r7.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is intercourse, in the prohibition against approaching wives during menstruation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القرب في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r8.claim: The second sense is answering: God's 'I am near' means that He responds, as does 'He is all-hearing, near.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القرب في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r9.claim: The third sense is nearness in time, in the soon-coming punishment and in the approaching Reckoning and true promise.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r9.anchor: والثالث : قرب الزمان . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r10.claim: The fourth sense is what is more correct, as in the seeker hoping to find a path closer to right guidance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r10.anchor: والرابع : الأصوب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الكهف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r11.claim: The fifth sense is gentleness or affection, describing the Christians as closest in affection to the believers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r11.anchor: والخامس : اللين . ومنه قوله تعالى في المائدة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r12.claim: The sixth sense is kinship, in the passages about affection for close relatives and feeding a poor person who is near of kin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r12.anchor: والسادس : القرابة . ومنه قوله تعالى في عسق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r13.claim: The seventh sense is a time just before the angel of death is seen, as in those who repent shortly before death.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r13.anchor: والسابع : ما قبل معاينة الملك . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r14.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r14.claim: The eighth sense is eating, as in the prohibition against Adam and Eve approaching the tree.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r14.anchor: والثامن : الأكل . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r15.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r15.claim: The ninth sense is entering prayer, as in the prohibition against approaching prayer while intoxicated.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p497/r15.anchor: والتاسع : الدخول في الصلاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p74/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p74/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses istajābah as answering; the cited verse of poetry uses it in the sense of answering a caller.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p74/r1.anchor:
أي: يجيبوني، هذا قول أبي عبيدة، وأنشد:
وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى ... فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب (2)

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r1.claim: A first parse makes ajību a nominative adjectival clause describing qarīb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب }: في " أجيب " وجهان أحدهما:

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r2.claim: Alternatively, ajību is a second predicate of innī, following qarīb as the first predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها خبر ثان لإني، لأن " قريب " خبر أول.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r3.claim: An implied command to speak follows the conditional fāʾ: say to them that God is near, since nearness is the condition's reported consequence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r3.anchor: ولا بد من إضمار قول بعد فاء الجزاء تقديره: فقل لهم إني قريب، وإنما احتجنا

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r4.claim: Ajību follows the pronoun preceding the predicate rather than switching to third-person agreement with qarīb, the more usual Arab pattern; the author cites Q 27:55, Q 27:47, and an unattributed poem.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r4.anchor: وجاء قوله " أجيب " مراعاة للضمير السابق على الخبر، ولم يراع الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r5.claim: The shift in ʿannī and innī moves from third-person reference to first-person speech; the preceding explicit name of God functions like a third-person pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r5.anchor: وفي قوله: { عني } و " إني " التفات من غيبة إلى تكلم، لأن قبله، " ولتكبروا الله "

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r6.claim: The kaf addresses the Prophet even though he is not named here; the earlier phrase about revelation implies that the Quran was sent down to the Messenger.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r6.anchor: والكاف في " سألك " للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن لم يجر له ذكر، إلا أن

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r7.claim: Nearness is metaphorical for the speed of answering a caller, since God transcends bodily proximity and place; Q 50:16 and the cited report illustrate the wording.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r7.anchor: وفي قوله: " فإني قريب " مجاز عن سرعة إجابته لدعوة داعيه، وإلا فهو متعال

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r8.claim: The second idhā may be a temporal adverb governed by ajību, meaning that He answers at the time of calling.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r8.anchor: والعامل في " إذا " قال الشيخ: " قوله: أجيب " يعني " إذا " الثانية

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r9.claim: The second idhā may instead be conditional, with its answer omitted as indicated by ajību, or ajību itself may be the answer under analyses allowing it before the condition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أن تكون لمجرد الظرفية وأن تكون شرطية، وحذف جوابها لدلالة " أجيب " عليه،

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r10.claim: The first idhā is governed by the implied speech verb, fa-qul, in the reconstructed sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r10.anchor: وأما " إذا " الأولى فإن العامل فيها ذلك القول المقدر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r11.claim: The tāʾ in daʿwa marks the verbal noun's form, not a single occurrence; like raḥma and najda, it does not make the noun singular in event count.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186/r11.anchor: والهاء في " دعوة " ليست الدالة على المرة نحو: ضربة وقتلة، بل التي بني عليها المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r1.claim: The two yāʾs are orthographic extra-letter variants absent from the codex form: readers omit them throughout, retain them in both positions, or retain them in connection but omit them at pause; the set has sixty-two yāʾs.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r1.anchor: والياءان من قوله: " الداع - دعان " من الزوائد عند القراء، ومعنى ذلك أن الصحابة لم تثبت

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Qālūn retain both yāʾs in connected reading and omit them at pause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r2.anchor: فأثبت أبو عمرو وقالون هاتين الياءين وصلا وحذفاها وقفا.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r3.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r3.claim: One analysis keeps the request sense of the istifʿāl form: let them ask for My response.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما: أنه للطلب على بابه، والمعنى: فليطلبوا إجابتي قاله ثعلب.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r4.claim: Istajāba can function like ajāba, with istifʿāl matching ifʿāl; the author lists several other paired forms as parallels.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنه بمعنى الإفعال، فيكون استفعل وأفعل بمعنى،

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r5.claim: In Quran usage istajāba appears with a preposition; an unattributed poem uses it transitively, though the author allows that a preposition may have been omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r5.anchor: ومن تعديه بنفسه قوله: 854 وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r6.claim: The lām in fa-l-yastajībū is the imperative lām.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r7.speaker: الرماني
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r7.claim: Al-Rummānī says istajāba entails accepting the invitation, while ajāba is broader and can answer by opposing it; he cites Q 21:76 and Q 3:195.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r7.anchor: وفرق الرماني بين أجاب واستجاب: بأن " استجاب " لا يكون إلا فيما

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r8.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r8.claim: The majority read yarshudūn with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḍamma on shīn, from the past form rasha-da with fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r8.anchor: والجمهور على " يرشدون " بفتح الياء وضم الشين، وماضيه رشد بالفتح

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r9.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla, with disagreement from one of them, read the shīn with kasra, from rashida with kasra in the past.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة بخلاف عنهما بكسر الشين،

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r10.claim: Another reported reading puts fatḥa on the shīn.

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r11.claim: A passive reading of yarshudūn is also reported.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r11.anchor: وماضيه رشد بالكسر، وقرىء، يرشدون " مبنيا للمفعول،

SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r12.claim: A reading with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on shīn derives from arshada; its object is omitted, understood as guiding others.
SAMIN-DURR:2:186#2/r12.anchor: وقرىء: " يرشدون " بضم الياء وكسر الشين من أرشد. المفعول على هذا محذوف

ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r4.claim: If asked where God is, He is near and no place is devoid of Him; Zajjāj supports this with the verses about God's presence in confidential conversation and being with people wherever they are.
ZAJJAJ:v1p254/r4.anchor: فالله عز وجل قريب لا يخلو منه مكان

ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r1.claim: One may pronounce daʿānī with yāʾ or omit the yāʾ; pausing follows the written muṣḥaf.
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r1.anchor: إن شئت قلت إذا دعاني بياء وإن شئت بغير ياء

ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r2.claim: One kind of calling on God is affirming His oneness and praising Him; the command to call in 40:60 includes this worship.
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r2.anchor: فضرب منها توحيده والثناء عليه كقولك يا الله لا إله إلا أنت

ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r3.claim: A second kind of duʿāʾ asks God for pardon, mercy, and related benefits.
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r3.anchor: وضرب ثان هو مسألة الله العفو والرحمة، وما يقرب منه

ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r4.claim: A third kind asks for worldly provisions such as wealth and children.
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r4.anchor: وضرب ثالث هو مسألته من الدنيا كقولك: اللهم ارزقني مالا وولدا

ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r5.claim: All three are called duʿāʾ because a person begins them by saying O Allah, O Lord, or O Ever-Living.
ZAJJAJ:v1p255/r5.anchor: وإنما سمي هذا أجمع دعاء لأن الإنسان يصدر في هذه الأشياء بقوله يا الله، ويا رب، ويا حي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r1.claim: The author rejects explaining Qur’anic deletion of final weak letters as rhyme or avoidance of adjacent sukūns; examples across the Qur’an show the grammar rules need testing against actual usage.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r1.anchor: ولا مجال لقولٍ في هذه الآيات ونظائرها، بحذف ياء المنقوص المضتف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r1.claim: The answer to the conditional precedes its condition, suggesting that God answers the servant even before the servant begins praying.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r1.anchor: تقدّم جواب الشرط على فعل الشرط ومعناه أن الله تعالى يجيب دعاء العبد حتى قبل أن يبدأ بالدعاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r2.claim: Unlike other question passages where the Messenger is told قل, God answers the servants directly here, with no intermediary, even the Prophet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r2.anchor: فقد جاء الردّ مباشرة من الله تعالى لعباده في خطاب مباشر ليس بين الله تعالى وعباده أي وسيط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r3.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r3.claim: Grammarians describe إذن as a response and a consequence, hence a conditional particle; it can also serve simply as a reply.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r3.anchor: (إذن) كما قال النحاة: هي حرف جواب وجزاء أي شرط.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r4.claim: The particle إذن may also be an ordinary response, as in the dialogue where one says “I love you” and the other answers “Then you are truthful.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r4.anchor: وأحياناً تكون إذن حرف جواب كأن نقول: قال أحبك، فيردّ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r6.claim: One view writes إذن with alif throughout because it is pronounced with alif when pausing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r6.anchor: بالألف مطلقاً لأنه يوقف عليها بالألف (إذا) وليس بالتنوين (إذاً)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r7.claim: A second view says the word is never written with nūn in the muṣḥaf.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r7.anchor: لم ترسم في المصحف بالنون أبداً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r8.speaker: قسم من النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r8.claim: Some say it is written with alif when it governs a subjunctive verb, but with nūn when it does not, avoiding confusion with إذا.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r8.anchor: قسم ذهب لأنه إذا نصبت المضارع رسمت بالألف لأنها عند ذلك لا تلتبس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r9.claim: Another stated convention is to write it with nūn outside the muṣḥaf.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r9.anchor: تكتب بالنون دائماً فيما عدا المصحف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r10.claim: A final view allows either spelling, with alif or nūn.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p647/r10.anchor: لنا أن نكتبها كما نشاء بالألف أو النون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r1.claim: Explicit ياء المتكلم in عبادي signals a wider addressed group; omitting it and marking it with kasra narrows the group. Such deletion is permitted in Arabic and can reflect scope or duration.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r1.anchor: وكلمة (عبادي) تدل على أن مجموعة العباد الذين يناديهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r3.claim: The explicit yā in عبادي suits the verse because every servant may ask God, so the address encompasses all servants.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p769/r3.anchor: جاءت (عبادي) بذكر ياء المتكلم لأنها تشمل كل العباد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r1.claim: In this usage, عبادي with yā denotes more people than عبادِ without it: all servants ask or face death, while the addressed muttaqūn and patient are a smaller group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1060/r1.anchor: إذن في القرآن الكريم حيث قال عبادي بالياء هم أكثر من عباد بدون ياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r1.claim: The general language rule uses feminine قريبة for kinship, while non-kinship proximity permits either masculine or feminine forms.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r1.anchor: أهل اللغة يقولون إذا كان القرب من النسب نقول قريبة مثل فلانة قريبتي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r2.claim: Though both genders are grammatically possible, the verse chooses masculine قريب; the author explains that an إضافة can take gender from its complement when it is part-like or nearly so.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r2.anchor: يكتسب المضاف من المضاف إليه بشروط معينة أن يكون جزءاً أو كاجزء في الاستغناء عنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r3.claim: A cited line predicates feminine شرقت of the masculine صدر because صدر القناة acquires feminine agreement from the genitive القناة.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r3.anchor: وتشرق بالأمر الذي أذعته كما شرقت صدر القناة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r4.claim: The line about the towers of the city likewise uses feminine تواضعت with masculine سور, attributing agreement to the feminine complement المدينة.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r4.anchor: (لما أتى خبر الزبير تواضعت سور المدينة) لم يقل تواضع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r5.claim: A cited line with رماح and الرياح is offered in the discussion of gender agreement in an إضافة construction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r5.anchor: مشينا كما اهتزت رماح تسفّهت أعاليها مرّ الرياح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r6.claim: The line وما حب الديار شغفن قلبي is another example in the author’s discussion of gender agreement influenced by an إضافة complement.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r6.anchor: وما حب الديار شغفن قلبي ولكن حب من سكن الديارا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r7.claim: Masculine قريب allows both God and His mercy to be understood as near; feminine قريبة would point only to mercy.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1078/r7.anchor: لو قال قريبة كانت تدل على الرحمة فقط لكن الله سبحانه وتعالى هو قريب

NASHR:v1p30/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p30/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p30/r1.claim: Al-Dānī says a single recitation transmits only some of the seven aḥruf, since one cannot simultaneously apply mutually exclusive vocalizations or word orders.
NASHR:v1p30/r1.anchor: قول أبي عمرو الداني إن الأحرف السبعة ليست متفرقة في القرآن كلها ولا موجودة فيه في ختمة واحدة

NASHR:v1p30/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p30/r2.speaker: جماعات من الفقهاء والقراء والمتكلمين
NASHR:v1p30/r2.claim: One scholarly camp holds that the ʿUthmānic codices contain all seven aḥruf, arguing that the community could not neglect any revealed letter and that the Companions agreed on the codices.
NASHR:v1p30/r2.anchor: ذهب جماعات من الفقهاء والقراء والمتكلمين إلى أن المصاحف العثمانية مشتملة على جميع الأحرف السبعة

NASHR:v1p30/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p30/r3.speaker: جماهير العلماء من السلف والخلف وأئمة المسلمين
NASHR:v1p30/r3.claim: The majority holds that the codices contain all seven aḥruf that their consonantal outlines can bear, covering the Prophet’s final presentation to Gabriel without omitting any letter.
NASHR:v1p30/r3.anchor: وذهب جماهير العلماء من السلف والخلف وأئمة المسلمين إلى أن هذه المصاحف العثمانية مشتملة على ما يحتمله رسمها من الأحرف السبعة

NASHR:v1p30/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p30/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p30/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī prefers the majority position, saying sound hadiths and widely transmitted reports support it; he promises a further qualification later in the chapter.
NASHR:v1p30/r4.anchor: وهذا القول هو الذي يظهر صوابه ; لأن الأحاديث الصحيحة والآثار المشهورة المستفيضة تدل عليه

NASHR:v1p30/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p30/r5.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
NASHR:v1p30/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others answer that reading all seven was a permission, not an obligation; the Companions could lawfully unite on one letter to prevent division and fighting.
NASHR:v1p30/r5.anchor: ما قاله الإمام المجتهد محمد بن جرير الطبري وغيره وهو أن القراءة على الأحرف السبعة

NASHR:v2p183/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وورش
NASHR:v2p183/r8.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Abū Jaʿfar, Yaʿqūb, and Warsh affirm the yāʾ in both occurrences of the phrase in al-Baqara.
NASHR:v2p183/r8.anchor: واتفق أبو عمرو وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وورش على الإثبات في الداع إذا دعاني كليهما في البقرة

NASHR:v2p183/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r9.speaker: أبو العلاء وأبو محمد
NASHR:v2p183/r9.claim: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ and Abū Muḥammad affirm both yāʾs for Qālūn through the ʿUthmānī route from Abū Nashīṭ.
NASHR:v2p183/r9.anchor: وقطع بالإثبات فيهما من طريق أبي نشيط الحافظ أبو العلاء، وفي غايته، وأبو محمد في مبهجه، وهي رواية العثماني عن قالون

NASHR:v2p183/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r10.speaker: الكفاية والجامع لابن فارس والمستنير والتجريد
NASHR:v2p183/r10.claim: These sources give Qālūn, by Abū Nashīṭ, affirmation in الداع and deletion in دعان; al-Mabhaj gives this pattern by Ibn Būyān from Abū Nashīṭ.
NASHR:v2p183/r10.anchor: وهو الذي في الكفاية في الست

NASHR:v2p183/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r11.speaker: التجريد والعنوان
NASHR:v2p183/r11.claim: Other sources give Qālūn the reverse pattern: deletion in الداع and affirmation in دعان, including al-Tajrīd through al-Ḥulwānī and Abū ʿAwn.
NASHR:v2p183/r11.anchor: فقطعوا له بالحذف في الداع والإثبات في دعان، وهو الذي في التجريد من طريق الحلواني

NASHR:v2p183/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p183/r12.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī accepts both patterns from Qālūn but prefers deletion as the more frequent and famous transmission.
NASHR:v2p183/r12.anchor: والوجهان صحيحان عن قالون إلا أن الحذف أكثر وأشهر

NASHR:v2p183/r13.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r13.speaker: المبهج عن الشذائي عن ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل
NASHR:v2p183/r13.claim: Al-Mabhaj reports affirmation in الداع for Qunbul through al-Shadhāʾī and Ibn Shanabūdh; Ibn al-Jazarī regards the attribution as doubtful.
NASHR:v2p183/r13.anchor: وذكر في المبهج الإثبات في الداع من طريق الشذائي عن ابن شنبوذ عن قنبل، وفيه نظر

NASHR:v2p183/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p183/r14.speaker: ابن شنبوذ عن ورش من طريق الأزرق
NASHR:v2p183/r14.claim: Ibn Shanabūdh reports deletion of the yāʾ in دعان for Warsh through al-Azraq; the excerpt breaks off as al-Dānī begins his comment.
NASHR:v2p183/r14.anchor: وذكر ابن شنبوذ عن ورش من طريق الأزرق الحذف في دعان قال الداني

NASHR:v2p236/r25.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r25.speaker: ورش
NASHR:v2p236/r25.claim: Warsh opens the yāʾ in وليؤمنوا بي.

NASHR:v2p236/r26.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r26.speaker: المدنيان وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p236/r26.claim: The two Medinan readers and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ in مني إلا.
NASHR:v2p236/r26.anchor: مني إلا فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو

NASHR:v2p236/r29.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r29.speaker: أبو عمرو وورش وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p236/r29.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Warsh, and Abū Jaʿfar affirm the yāʾ in الداع at continuation; Yaʿqūb affirms it both at pause and continuation, while Qālūn differs as noted earlier.
NASHR:v2p236/r29.anchor: الداع إذا أثبت الباء في الوصل أبو عمرو وورش وأبو جعفر، واختلف عن قالون كما تقدم

NASHR:v2p236/r30.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r30.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وورش ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p236/r30.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr, and Warsh affirm the yāʾ in دعان at continuation; Yaʿqūb affirms it in both positions, while Qālūn differs as noted earlier.
NASHR:v2p236/r30.anchor: دعان أثبت الياء فيها وصلا أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وورش، واختلف عن قالون كما تقدم وأثبتها في الحالتين يعقوب

NASHR:v2p171#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p171#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p171#2/r1.claim: Of thirty disputed yāʾs in this category, two occur in al-Baqara: بيتي للطائفين and بي لعلهم يرشدون.
NASHR:v2p171#2/r1.anchor: وهي في البقرة ثنتان بيتي للطائفين، وبي لعلهم يرشدون

NASHR:v2p171#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p171#2/r3.speaker: ورش
NASHR:v2p171#2/r3.claim: Warsh opens the yāʾ in بي لعلهم in al-Baqara and in لي فاعتزلون in al-Dukhān.
NASHR:v2p171#2/r3.anchor: بي لعلهم في البقرة ولي فاعتزلون في الدخان

QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#1/r1.claim: Some readers pause without the final yāʾ while others restore it in both words; the full form makes God's first person object explicit.
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: some readers pause on dāʿ/daʿān (without yāʾ) or restore full yāʾ on both

QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#2/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#2/r1.claim: The ten-reader form retains final yāʾ in both words, making the first-person object Me explicit rather than implied.
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:11#2/r1.anchor: Ten-reader variant: full yāʾ on both words. Makes the ""Me"" (nī) in daʿānī fully explicit

QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#1/r1.claim: The variant cluster also affects daʿānī: the pausal form drops the nūn of protection, while the full form restores the first person suffix.
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#1/r1.anchor: See word 11 — same variant cluster affects daʿāni. Pausal form daʿān strips the nūn of wiqāya

QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#2/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#2/r1.claim: The ten-reader form restores final yāʾ and the explicit first person object suffix Me.
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:13#2/r1.anchor: Ten-reader: full yāʾ restoring explicit ""Me"" suffix.

QIRAAT-ER:2:186:21#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:21#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:21#1/r1.claim: A fatḥa on the yāʾ is grammatically valid alongside bī and adds phonetic weight to the divine self-reference.
QIRAAT-ER:2:186:21#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: fatḥa on yāʾ (biya vs bī). Grammatically both valid for preposition + 1sg pronoun

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p73/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p73/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p73/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the Prophet’s Companions asked him where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed in response.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p73/r1.anchor: عن عوف عن الحسن قال سأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا أين ربنا فأنزل الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reports that people, identified variously as Jews or believers, asked the Prophet whether their Lord was near enough for private speech or far enough to require calling aloud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r4.anchor: أن قوما، قيل: اليهود، وقيل: المؤمنون، قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أقريب ربنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r5.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says that after “Call upon Me, I will answer you” was revealed, people asked when they should pray, and this verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء: لما نزل. وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم قال قوم: في أي ساعة ندعو؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r6.claim: After commanding glorification and gratitude for guidance, God says He sees those who remember and thank Him, hears their calls, and answers their prayers or requests; invocation should begin with praise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r6.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه تعالى لما تضمن قوله: ولتكبروا الله على ما هداكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r7.claim: The second-person address is to the Prophet although he is not named in the wording, since the preceding account presupposes that the Qur’an was revealed to God’s Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r7.anchor: والكاف في: سألك، خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وإن لم يجر له ذكر في اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r8.claim: “My servants” is apparently general, though some restrict it to Jews or to believers according to the disputed occasion of revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r8.anchor: و: عبادي، ظاهره العموم، وقيل: أريد به الخصوص:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r9.claim: The pronoun refers to God; “about Me” shifts from the preceding third-person mention of God to first person, and is governed by “asked.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r9.anchor: و: عني، فالضمير فيه لله تعالى، وهو من باب الالتفات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r10.claim: God’s nearness cannot be spatial; it means He hears invocation and promptly grants the petitioner’s request, figuratively like someone nearby who quickly answers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p204/r10.anchor: والقرب المنسوب إلى الله تعالى يستحيل أن يكون قربا بالمكان، وإنما القرب هنا عبارة عن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.claim: The shift to addressing the Prophet while speaking of “My servants” honors him and raises his rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r1.anchor: في تلوين الخطاب مع توجيهه لسيد ذوي الألباب عليه الصلاة والسلام ما لا يخفى من التشريف ورفع المحل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.claim: The question concerns God's nearness or distance, not His essence.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r2.anchor: عني أي عن قربي وبعدي إذ ليس السؤال عن ذاته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.claim: An omitted command to tell them is required for the conditional answer to follow; its omission shows God undertook the answer Himself rather than leaving it to the Messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r3.anchor: أي فقل لهم ذلك بأن تخبر عن القرب بأي طريق كان ولا بد من التقدير إذ بدونه لا يترتب على الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.claim: God's nearness is metaphorical, since spatial proximity is impossible for Him; it denotes His knowledge of servants' acts and words and awareness of their states.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r4.anchor: والقرب حقيقة في القرب المكاني المنزه عنه تعالى فهو استعارة لعلمه تعالى بأفعال العباد وأقوالهم وإطلاعه على سائر أحوالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna and Abdullah ibn Ahmad report from Ubayy that Muslims asked whether their Lord was near enough for private conversation or far enough to require calling aloud, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي قال : قال المسلمون يارسول الله أقريب ربنا فنناجيه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.claim: God's answering the supplicant explains and confirms His nearness; the direct transition conveys intimacy, and “when” promises an answer in general rather than a guaranteed fulfillment of every request.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r6.anchor: دليل للقرب وتقرير له فالقطع لكمال الاتصال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi sees no need to qualify the promise by God's will, redefine answering as merely “Here I am,” or restrict it to sinless requests or obedient supplicants, though piety helps.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r7.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى التقييد بالمشيئة المؤذن به قوله تعالى في آية أخرى : ( فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.claim: A devout, humble supplicant is more likely to receive an answer, especially at particular times, places, and in recognized ways.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r8.anchor: نعم كونه كذلك أزجى للإجابة لا سيما في الأزمنة المخصوصة والأمكنة المعلومة والكيفية المشهورة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.claim: In a sound report from Abu Sa'id, the Prophet says a Muslim's lawful supplication brings one of three outcomes: immediate answer, deferred reward, or protection from equivalent harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r9.anchor: في الصحيح عن أبي سعيد قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.claim: “Let them respond to Me” may mean ask Me to answer their prayers, or answer My call to faith and obedience as I answer their needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r10.anchor: أي فليطلبوا إجابتي لهم إذا دعوني أو فليجيبوا لي إذا دعوتهم للإيمان والطاعة كما أني أجيبهم إذا دعوني لحوائجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.claim: Most commentators take the command to mean that people should answer God's call to faith and obedience; “believe in Me” then calls for steadfastness in faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r11.anchor: وهذا ما عليه أكثر المفسرين ولا يغني عنه وليؤمنوا بي لأنه أمر بالثبات والمداومة على الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.claim: The command to believe is not redundant with responding to God: it commands persistence and constancy in faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r12.anchor: ولا يغني عنه وليؤمنوا بي لأنه أمر بالثبات والمداومة على الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r13.claim: “Perhaps they will be rightly guided” means guided to the interests of their religion and worldly life; the root sense is attaining good.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r13.anchor: أي يهتدون لمصالح دينهم ودنياهم وأصل الباب إصابة الخير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r14.claim: The word is also read with the shin vowel opened or kasra-marked.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r14.anchor: وقريء بفتح الشين وكسرها ولما أمرهم سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r15.claim: After the commands about fasting the month, counting its days, and magnifying and thanking God, this verse stresses that He knows deeds, hears words, and repays them; alternatively, amid abrogation it reassures believers of His knowledge, power, and kindness.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p63#2/r15.anchor: ولما أمرهم سبحانه وتعالى بصوم الشهر ومراعاة العدة وحثهم على القيام بوظائف التكبير والشكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, reports Ibn Abbas's occasion: Jews of Medina asked how God could hear when they claimed the distance to heaven was a 500-year journey and each heaven was equally thick.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r1.anchor: روى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال يهود أهل المدينة: يا محمد كيف يسمع ربنا دعاءنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r2.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says some Companions asked whether their Lord was near, so they should speak privately, or far, so they should call aloud.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: سأل بعض الصحابة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r3.claim: An omitted instruction is understood: tell them God is near to them in knowledge, with nothing hidden from Him; the same idea appears at 50:16.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r3.anchor: ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r4.claim: During the expedition toward Khaybar, Abū Mūsā says people loudly called takbīr from a valley; the Prophet told them to moderate, since they call One who hears and is near, not deaf or absent, and He is with them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p204/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: لما غزا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خيبر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة غير قالون وأبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r1.claim: Medinan readers other than Qālūn, along with Abū ʿAmr, retain the two yāʾs in connected recitation; the others omit them in connected and paused recitation. Yaʿqūb retains all deleted yāʾs in both positions, and readers agree on retaining those written in the script.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة غير قالون وأبو عمرو بإثبات الياء فيهما في الوصل، والباقون بحذفها وصلا ووقفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r2.claim: One reading of istijāba is “answer me,” meaning obey me; answering can mean obedience or granting a request, while God's answering is giving and the servant's answering is obedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r2.anchor: قيل: الاستجابة بمعنى الإجابة، أي: فليجيبوا لي بالطاعة، والإجابة في اللغة: الطاعة وإعطاء ما سئل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r3.claim: Another reading is “ask Me to answer”; in substance, the instruction is to obey God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r3.anchor: وقيل: فليستجيبوا لي أي ليستدعوا مني الإجابة، وحقيقته فليطيعوني

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r4.claim: The purpose is that they be guided.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r5.claim: To explain why many prayers seem unanswered despite this promise, one view takes supplication here as obedience and response as reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r5.anchor: قيل معنى الدعاء ههنا الطاعة، ومعنى الإجابة الثواب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r6.claim: Other explanations limit the general wording: God answers if He wills, if the request accords with the decree, if the answer is good for the petitioner, or if the request is not impossible; the first is compared to 6:41.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r6.anchor: قيل معنى الآيتين خاص وإن كان لفظهما عاما، تقديرهما: {أجيب دعوة الداع} إن شئت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r7.claim: The Prophet says God answers so long as a person does not pray for sin or severing kinship and does not become impatient; impatience is repeating the plea, seeing no answer, despairing, and abandoning prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r8.claim: One general reading takes “I answer” to mean “I hear”; the verse promises an answer to the call, not necessarily the requested object, just as a master can answer a servant without granting the request.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r8.anchor: وقيل هو عام، ومعنى قوله {أجيب} أي أسمع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r9.claim: Another explanation says God never frustrates a prayer: He grants the requested matter if decreed, otherwise stores its reward for the Hereafter or averts harm; a report from ʿUbāda supports this.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r9.anchor: وقيل معنى الآية أنه لا يخيب دعاءه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r10.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r10.claim: The Prophet says no Muslim prays without receiving what he asked or having equivalent harm averted, unless he asks for sin or severing kinship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r10.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت رضي الله عنه حدثهم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r11.claim: One view says God answers the believer promptly but delays granting the request so He may hear the believer's voice, while He hastens the disliked person's request because He dislikes hearing that voice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى يجيب دعاء المؤمن في الوقت ويؤخر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r12.claim: Supplication has manners and conditions that cause acceptance; those who fulfill them are eligible for an answer, while those who violate them transgress and do not deserve one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p205/r12.anchor: وقيل: إن للدعاء آدابا وشرائط وهي أسباب الإجابة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r4.claim: The opening “and when” continues an unstated sequence: after Ramadan fasting and Laylat al-Qadr, the supplication of fasting people is especially likely to be answered.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r4.anchor: ولما كان دعاء الصائم مجانا وكان هذا الشهر بالخصوص مظنة الإجابة للصيام ولمكان ليلة القدر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r5.claim: Because God's majesty may suggest the distance of an earthly king, the transition reassures servants that He watches both the obedient and disobedient and is near.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r5.anchor: وكان ذكر كبريائه سبحانه وتعالى مهيئا لعباده للإحساس بالبعد فكان ربما أوقع في وهم أنه على عادة المتكبرين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī portrays fasting as a path to hidden reward and a glimpse of God's kingdom in Laylat al-Qadr; the resulting blessings make people at successive spiritual ranks ask what the servants received.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r6.anchor: لما أثبت الحق سبحانه وتعالى كتاب الصيام لعباده لما أرادهم له نم إعلائهم إلى خبء جزائه وأطلعهم على ما شاء في صومهم من ملكوته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r7.speaker: عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r7.claim: ʿUmar reports that the Prophet and Abū Bakr once spoke as though in a foreign tongue that ʿUmar could not understand, illustrating their different spiritual rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r7.anchor: يؤثر عن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : ( كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يكلم أبا بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the servants’ question as whether God is remote like earthly kings, in the spiritual setting opened by fasting and its hidden reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r8.anchor: وقال الحرالي : لما أثبت الحق سبحانه وتعالى كتاب الصيام لعباده لما أرادهم له نم إعلائهم إلى خبء جزائه وأطلعهم على ما شاء في صومهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r9.claim: God answers in the first person directly rather than telling the Prophet to say the answer; this removes the impression of distance and signals His exceptional nearness and presence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r9.anchor: فإني } دون فقل إني , فإنه لو أثبت قل , لأوهم بعدا وليس المقام كذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r10.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r10.claim: Al-Qushayrī says questions about mountains, orphans, menstruation, and crescents receive an intermediary, but those asking about God have the intermediaries removed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r10.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري ما معناه : الذين يسألون عن الجبال وعن اليتامى وعن المحيض وعن الأهلة ونحوها يجابون بالواسطة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r11.speaker: ناصر الدين بن ميلق
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r11.claim: Nāṣir al-Dīn ibn Milayq says direct divine speech suits a God already known through His acts, signs, and innate reason; moons and similar matters require the Prophet to convey what reason cannot know.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r11.anchor: وقال الإمام قاضي القضاة ناصر الدين بن ميلق ما معناه : إنه سبحانه وتعالى لما كان قد تعرف إلى عباده بأفعاله وآياته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r12.claim: Qarīb is an intensive form from the root for nearness: one who seeks God through reason finds and knows Him; revelation gives further recognition and relieves hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r12.anchor: فعيل من القرب وهو مطالعة الشيء حسا أو معنى أي من طلبني بعقله وجدني وعرفني

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r13.claim: Omitting “say” hastens recognition and strengthens the status of the messenger, since a quick answer better demonstrates his truthfulness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r13.anchor: وإسقاط قل , أسرع في التعرف فهو أجدر بتعظيم الواسطة لأن الإسراع في الإجابة أقرب دلالة على صدقه في الرسالة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r14.claim: Al-Ḥarālī denies physical distance or proximity for God; spiritual nearness depends on hearing God's own address, while mediation through sensory experience makes one more distant in degree.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p347/r14.anchor: ومعلوم أن قرب الله وبعد المخلوق منه ليس بعد مسافة ولا قرب مسافة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r1.claim: Biqai cites the Prophet’s duty of communication to frame his recitation as conveying God’s own message directly to the community.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r1.anchor: إنما عليك البلاغ } ) 77 [ الرعد : 40 ] وكان أن ما يتلوه لأمته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the Prophet recites God's words so the community hears its Lord directly; the Prophet connects servants to God rather than standing as a barrier between them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r2.anchor: إنما هو كلام ربه يتلو لهم كلام ربهم ليسمعوه من ربهم لأمته حتى لا يكون صلى الله عليه وسلم واسطة بين العبد وربه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees the Qur’an’s repeated “say” as an explicit cue that anyone hearing it is listening to God's speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r3.anchor: وللإشارة بهذا المعنى يتلى كلمة قل , في القرآن ليكون إفصاحا لسماع كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى ممن سمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r4.claim: The verse foreshadows Hajj: Eid follows the fasting month just as the pilgrimage season follows, implicitly raising Abraham's call and preparing the sūra’s integrated account of pilgrimage.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r4.anchor: وفي إشعاره إهزاز القلوب والأسماع إلى نداء الحج إثر الصوم , لأنه جعل تعالى أول يوم من شهور الحج إثر يوم من أيام الصوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r5.claim: Biqai glosses ijāba as meeting through speech, the first step toward a complete encounter face to face.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r5.anchor: أجيب } من الإجابة وهي اللقاء بالقول ابتداء شروع لتمام اللقاء بالمواجهة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī connects answered prayer to the pilgrim’s call at the end of fasting: fasting resembles erasure and the intermediate state, while Hajj resembles a detached journey and resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r6.anchor: فإن حال الصوم التابع لآية الموت في كونه محوا لحال البرزخ وحال الحج في كونه سفرا إلى مكان مخصوص

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes Eid as the transition from retreat and worship in God's house to the place of divine manifestation in Hajj.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r7.anchor: ليكون انتقالهم من بيت خلوته بالعكوف إلى موقف تجليه في الحج

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says God answers a servant whose inner state is sound rather than driven by appetite; otherwise the prayer is stored for later or expiates sins, as the Prophet explained.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r8.anchor: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى يجيب دعوة العبد إذا كان فيه رشد وإلا ادخرها له أو كفر بها عنه كما بينه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r9.claim: Every creature inwardly calls through need even without speech; the explicit clause requires spoken supplication to match the sincerity of that inward state.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r9.anchor: ولما كان كل خلق داعيا لحاجته وإن لم ينطق بها أشار تعالى إلى مقصد إظهار الدعاء مقالا وابتهالا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r10.claim: Biqai notes readings that omit the two yāʾ letters, retaining only their kasra, and readings that pronounce both fully; he attributes the variation to Arab tribal speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p348/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة الاكتفاء بكسرة { الداع } و { دعان } عن ياءيهما وقراءة تمكينهما توسعة القراءة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r1.claim: Biqai invokes the Qur’an’s statement that it has been made easy for remembrance in support of the call to respond to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r1.anchor: { ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r2.claim: If a self-sufficient master undertakes to answer a servant, the needy servant has still greater reason to answer the master's summons.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r2.anchor: بأن السيد إذا التزم إجابة عبده كان إجابة العبد لسيده أوجب التزاما لاستغناء السيد وحاجة العبد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says istifʿāl suggests extracting compliance from a resistant soul, which resists the demanding journey to God's House.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r3.anchor: وجاء بصيغة الاستفعال المشعر باستخراج الإجابة مما شأنه الإباء لما في الأنفس من كره فيما تحمل عليه من الوصول إلى بيت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r4.claim: The response answers God's call to nearness and to His House, prompted by the servants’ innate need for Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r4.anchor: إنباء عما قد دعاهم إليه من قربه وقصد بيته بما جبلهم عليه من حاجتهم إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r5.claim: After commanding response to every divine call, Biqai presents faith as the first and foremost level, addressing believers and others; faith itself has indefinitely many degrees of strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r5.anchor: وكانت الاستجابةبالإيمان أول المراتب وأولاها وكانت مراتب الإيمان في قوته وضعفه لا تكاد تتناهى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r6.claim: The purpose is that people may continue to attain their goals and find the path of truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r6.anchor: أي ليكونوا على رجاء من الدوام على إصابة المقاصد والاهتداء إلى طريق الحق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines rushd as sound management of an affair, materially or spiritually, in religion or worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r7.anchor: والرشد حسن التصرف في الأمر حسا أو معنى في دين أو دنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the verse embraces the wayfarer’s whole course: repentance from distance, travel along the path of nearness, and eventual arrival to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p349/r8.anchor: ومن مقتضى هذه الآية تتفضل جميع أحوال السالكين إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى من توبة التائب من حد بعده إلى سلوك سبيل قربه

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r1.speaker: عن جده
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r1.claim: An Anṣārī man asked whether God was near enough for whispered prayer or far away and requiring a call; the Prophet was silent, then the verse was revealed, promising a response when they pray.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r1.anchor: عن رجل من الأنصار عن أبيه عن جده قال جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
