DURR-FULL:v1p469/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet’s Companions asked where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال سأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r3.claim: Anas reports that a Bedouin asked where God was; the Prophet answered that He was in heaven upon His Throne, recited 20:5, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r3.anchor: عن أنس قال سأل أعرابي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r4.claim: In Anas’s report, the Prophet answers the question about God’s whereabouts by saying He is in heaven upon the Throne, citing the Throne verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r4.anchor: قال: في السماء على عرشه ثم تلا (الرحمن على العرش استوى)

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r5.claim: Ali reports that after the Prophet urged people not to tire of prayer and cited 40:60, a man asked whether God hears supplication; this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r5.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تعجزوا عن الدعاء

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r6.claim: When 40:60 was revealed, people reportedly asked when to pray; this verse was then revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r6.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح أنه بلغه لما أنزلت

DURR-FULL:v1p469/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r7.speaker: سفيان عن أبي
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r7.claim: Sufyan transmits from his father that Muslims asked whether God was near for whispered prayer or far away, and this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p469/r7.anchor: من طريق سفيان عن أبي قال قال المسلمون يا رسول الله أقريب ربنا

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r1.claim: When 40:60 was revealed, people asked how they could reach God to call upon Him; this verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r2.claim: After the verse’s revelation, the people reportedly affirmed that their Lord was truthful and everywhere.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r2.anchor: فقالوا: صدق ربنا وهو بكل مكان

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses responding to God as obeying Him, and explains that istijāba here means obedience.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: قال المسلمون: أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses believing in God here as knowing Him.

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r5.claim: Al-Hasan gives an aphorism: ships are the keys to the seas, roads to the earth, and supplication to heaven.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال: مفتاح البحار السفن ومفتاح الأرض

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r6.claim: Kaʿb reports that Moses asked whether God was near or far; God said He accompanies whoever remembers Him and told Moses to remember Him in every state, including ritual impurity and relieving himself.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r6.anchor: عن كعب قال: قال موسى: أي رب أقريب أنت

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r7.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r7.claim: During an expedition, the Prophet told companions to lower their voices: they called upon One who hears and sees, is neither deaf nor absent, and is nearer than a mount’s neck.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r7.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة فجعلنا لا نصعد شرفا

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r8.speaker: أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r8.claim: Anas reports God’s words: He is as His servant expects and is with the servant when called upon.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r8.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال يقول الله: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي

DURR-FULL:v1p470/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r9.speaker: سلمان الفارسي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r9.claim: Salman reports that God is Living and Generous and is shy to return a servant’s raised hands empty; al-Tirmidhi graded the report good and al-Hakim called it sound.
DURR-FULL:v1p470/r9.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن ربكم حي كريم يستحي من عبده إذا رفع يديه إليه أن يردهما صفرا

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r1.speaker: معاذ بن جبل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r1.claim: Muʿadh reports the Prophet saying that with true knowledge of God, mountains would move in response to one’s supplication.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لو عرفتم الله حق معرفته

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r2.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r2.claim: Abu Dharr says that supplication alongside righteousness is as sufficient as salt in food.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: يكفي من الدعاء مع البر ما يكفي الطعام من الملح

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن شبيب
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r3.claim: When ʿAbd Allah ibn Shabib prayed aloud beside Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Saʿid rebuked him for acting as if God were not near.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شبيب قال: صليت إلى جنب سعيد بن المسيب المغرب

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r4.speaker: ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that whoever is granted an opening in supplication is granted the doors of response; al-Tirmidhi’s wording adds that the doors of mercy open and asking for well-being is especially beloved.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من فتح له في الدعاء

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r5.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r5.claim: A saying transmitted by Ibrahim al-Taymi holds that one who praises God before supplicating has secured a response, while one who supplicates first remains hopeful.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r5.anchor: عن إبراهيم التيمي قال: كان يقال: إذا بدأ الرجل بالثناء

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r6.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r6.claim: Salman reports God saying at Adam’s creation that the servant asks and supplicates, while God answers.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r6.anchor: عن سلمان قال: لما خلق الله آدم قال: واحدة لي وواحدة لك

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r7.speaker: نافع بن معد يكرب
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r7.claim: Nafiʿ ibn Maʿd Yakrib reports that ʿAʾisha asked the Prophet about the verse; Gabriel conveyed God’s greeting and promise to answer her sincere, pious prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r7.anchor: عن نافع بن معد يكرب قال: كنت أنا وعائشة فقالت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p473/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas transmits Jābir’s report that the Prophet recited the verse and then prayed with the talbiya, affirmations of God’s oneness, the afterlife, Paradise, Hell, the Hour, and resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v1p473/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r1.speaker: جد الصلب بن الحكيم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r1.claim: A man asks whether God is near, so they may speak privately, or far, so they must call aloud; after the Prophet is silent, the verse is revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r1.anchor: عن الصلب بن الحكيم عن أبيه عن جده قال : جاء رجل إلى رسول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r2.claim: The report glosses the command as God’s asking people to call on Him and believe in Him when He commands them to pray, promising a response.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r2.anchor: اذا امرتهم ان يدعوني فدعوني استجبت لهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says every believing servant’s prayer is answered: God grants worldly provision, stores it for the Resurrection, or averts harm.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r3.anchor: عن السدى واذا سالك عبادي عني فاني قريب اجيب دعوة الداع اذا دعان قال : ليس من عبد مؤمن يدعو الله الا استجاب له

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r4.claim: Anas explains “let them respond to Me” as “let them call upon Me.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r4.anchor: عن انس بن مالك في قول الله فليستجيبوا لي قال : ليدعوني

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says responding means obeying God; al-Rabiʿ and Ibn Jurayj are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد فليستجيبوا لي : فليطيعوني الاستجابة : الطاعة . وروي عن الربيع بن انس وابن جريج نحو قول مجاهد

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r6.claim: Anas explains belief in God here as their knowing that when they call on Him, He answers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي رجاء عن انس ابن مالك في قول الله وليؤمنوا بي انهم اذا دعوني استجبت لهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses “that they may be rightly guided” as “that they may be guided.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p314#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية لعلهم يرشدون يعني : يهتدون .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r1.claim: Answering a supplicant is God's favor, but this statement does not promise an answer to every person at every time; the conditional concerns being asked about God, not a universal guarantee tied to each invocation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r1.anchor: الآية دلت على أن إجابة دعاء الداعي تفضل من الله على عباده غير أن ذلك لا يقتضي التزام إجابة الدعوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r2.claim: The conditional links the response to the Prophet's being asked, rather than making a general if-they-invoke-me-then-I-answer promise; the verse does not say that formulation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r2.anchor: لأن الشرط هنا ربط الجواب بالسؤال وليس ربط للدعاء بالإجابة ، لأنه لم يقل : إن دعوني أجبتهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r3.claim: Since God answers supplication, people should answer His commands; istajāba and ajāba are synonymous, first meaning to come when called and then metaphorically to fulfill a request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r3.anchor: وقوله : { فليستجيبوا لي } تفريع على { أجيب } أي إذا كنت أجيب دعوة الداعي فليجيبوا أوامري ، واستجاب وأجاب بمعنى واحد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r4.claim: One reading takes responding as obeying God's commands, with believing separately enjoining continued faith: the first concerns action and the second its persistence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r4.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون المراد بالاستجابة امتثال أمر الله فيكون { وليؤمنوا بي } عطفا مغايرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r5.claim: Alternatively, responding includes accepting the invitation to faith, and the following command to believe singles out that especially important part of the general response.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالاستجابة ما يشمل استجابة دعوة الإيمان ، فذكر { وليؤمنوا } عطف خاص على عام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.claim: Rushd means attaining what is right; the verb is attested in forms patterned like nasara, fariha, and ḍaraba, with the first the most common.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p180#2/r1.anchor: والرشد إصابة الحق وفعله كنصر وفرح وضرب ، والأشهر الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r10.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says people asked whether their Lord was near, so they could speak privately, or distant, so they should call aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r10.anchor: قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: سببها أن قوما قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أقريب ربنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r11.speaker: عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r11.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked when they should pray, prompting this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r11.anchor: وقال عطاء: لما نزلت وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم [غافر: 60] قال قوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r12.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r12.claim: Mujahid says the question was where to direct supplication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بل قالوا إلى أين ندعو فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r13.claim: Qatada says the people asked how they should supplicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة بل قالوا: كيف ندعو؟ فنزلت وإذا سألك عبادي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r14.speaker: المشركون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r14.claim: The polytheists objected that God could not be near when seven immense heavens lay between them and Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r14.anchor: روي أن المشركين قالوا لما نزل فإني قريب: كيف يكون قريبا وبيننا وبينه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r15.claim: God is near in His ability and in answering supplication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r15.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان أي فإني قريب بالإجابة والقدرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r16.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r16.claim: One interpretation qualifies the promise: God answers if He wills.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r16.anchor: وقال قوم: المعنى أجيب إن شئت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r17.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r17.claim: Another view says each supplication receives one of three outcomes: a worldly answer, expiation, or reward stored for the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r17.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الله تعالى يجيب كل الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r18.claim: These outcomes apply when supplication stays within bounds; transgression in prayer is forbidden and 7:55 forbids it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p255/r18.anchor: وهذا إذا كان الدعاء على ما يجب دون اعتداء، فإن الاعتداء في الدعاء ممنوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r1.claim: Calling someone whose prayers are answered praises sound judgment and avoidance of transgression; God enables prayer for what is possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r1.anchor: والوصف بمجاب الدعوة: وصف بحسن النظر والبعد عن الاعتداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r2.claim: The Prophet prayed that his community would not fight among themselves, but that prayer was denied because destiny had decreed otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r2.anchor: وانظر أن أفضل البشر المصطفى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قد دعا أن لا يجعل بأس أمته بينهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r3.speaker: أبو رجاء الخراساني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r3.claim: Abu Raja al-Khurasani understands the command as “let them supplicate to Me.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r3.anchor: قال أبو رجاء الخراساني: «معناه فليدعوا لي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r4.claim: The author reads istajāba as “seek that I answer them,” following the request sense of istifʿāl, with rare exceptions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: المعنى فليطلبوا أن أجيبهم، وهذا هو باب استفعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r5.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r5.claim: Mujahid and others understand the command as answering God’s call to faith through obedience and action.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المعنى فليجيبوا لي فيما دعوتهم إليه من الإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r6.claim: Ajāba and istajāba can be synonymous; a poetic line uses istajāba to mean answer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r6.anchor: ويقال: أجاب واستجاب بمعنى، ومنه قول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r7.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r7.claim: Abu Raja takes “believe in Me” to mean believing that God answers their supplications.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وليؤمنوا بي، قال أبو رجاء: في أني أجيب دعاءهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r8.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r8.claim: Another interpretation treats the phrase as a call to faith generally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: بل ذلك دعاء إلى الإيمان بجملته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r9.claim: The majority read yarshudūn with open yāʾ and ḍamma on shīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يرشدون بفتح الياء وضم الشين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r10.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r10.claim: Some use ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on shīn; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Abu Haywa also transmit open yāʾ with kasra on shīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p256/r10.anchor: وقرأ قوم بضم الياء وفتح الشين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r1.speaker: جد الصلت بن حكيم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r1.claim: A Bedouin asked the Prophet whether God was near, so they could whisper to Him, or far, so they should call aloud; the report comes through al-Salt ibn Hakim, his father, and grandfather.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r1.anchor: أحدها أن أعرابيا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه فنزلت هذه الآية رواه الصلت بن حكيم عن أبيه عن جده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r2.claim: According to Ibn Abbas, Jews in Medina asked how God could hear them when, Muhammad claimed, the sky was a journey of five hundred years away.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r2.anchor: والثاني أن يهود المدينة قالوا يا محمد كيف يسمع ربنا دعاءنا وأنت تتزعم أن بيننا وبين السماء مسيرة خمسمائة عام فنزلت هذه الآية رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r3.claim: A third report says the Companions asked to be told which hour God most loves for supplication.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r3.anchor: أحب إلى الله أن ندعو فيها دعوانا فنزلت هذه الآية قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the Companions asked the Messenger where God is.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r4.anchor: والرابع أن أصحاب النبي قالوا له أين الله فنزلت هذه الآية قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r5.claim: Muqatil connects the verse to early fasting rules: after sleeping, one man ate and another had intercourse, then they asked how to repent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r5.anchor: فسألوا كيف التوبة مما عملوا فنزلت هذه الآية قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r6.claim: The instruction is to tell them that God is near when they ask about Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r6.anchor: ومعنى الكلام إذا سألوك عني فأعلمهم أني قريب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r7.speaker: الفراء وابن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r7.claim: Al-Farra and Ibn al-Qasim explain ujibu as “I hear.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r7.anchor: قولان أحدهما اسمع قاله الفراء وابن القاسم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda, Ibn Qutayba, and al-Zajjaj take ujibu as “I answer”; the command falyastajibū therefore means “let them answer Me,” supported by a poem using istajaba for answering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r8.anchor: أراد فلم يجبه وهذا قول أبي عبيدة وابن قتبية و الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliya says yurshadun means “they are guided.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r9.anchor: ﴿ لعلهم يرشدون ﴾ قال أبوالعالية يعني يهتدون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r10.speaker: النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r10.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim's lawful supplication is answered in one of three ways: granted promptly, stored for the afterlife, or matched by an equivalent harm averted; Abu Saʿid transmits the report.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r10.anchor: أن أبا سعيد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال ما من مسلم دعا الله تعالى بدعوة ليس فيها قطيعة رحم ولا إثم إلا أعطاه الله بها إحدى ثلاث خصال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r11.claim: Another answer is that supplication requires conditions rooted in obedience, including lawful food and a present heart; unlawful food blocks its answer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p189/r11.anchor: ومنها أكل الحلال فإن أكل الحرام يمنع إجابة الدعاء ومنها حضور القلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p190/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p190/r1.claim: A supplicant may mistake the requested outcome for what is best; God answers the deeper request for benefit, which may require delay or withholding.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p190/r1.anchor: وجواب آخر وهو أن الداعي قد يعتقد المصلحة في إجابته إلى ما سأل وقد لا تكون المصلحة في ذلك فيجاب إلى مقصوده الأصلي وهو طلب المصلحة وقد تكون المصلحة في التأخير أو في المنع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r1.speaker: أعرابي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim reports that a Bedouin asked whether the Lord was near, so they could whisper, or distant, so they should call aloud; the Prophet was silent and this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r1.anchor: عن جده، أن أعرابيا قال: يا رسول الله، أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Companions asked the Prophet where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: سأل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked when they should supplicate, and this verse followed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن عطاء: أنه بلغه لما نزلت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r4.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that during a campaign the Prophet told the Companions to lower their voices: they call one who hears and sees, not one deaf or absent, and is nearer than a rider’s mount’s neck; he then taught them that there is no might or power except through God, a treasure of Paradise. The report is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and other collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري، قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r5.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet quoted God as saying, ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p505#3/r5.anchor: حدثنا شعبة، حدثنا قتادة، عن أنس رضي الله عنه: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports God’s promise to be with His servant while the servant remembers Him and moves his lips in remembrance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r1.anchor: عن كريمة بنت الخشخاش المزنية، قالت: حدثنا أبو هريرة: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr links this assurance of divine company to God’s being with the pious and doers of good, and His promise to Moses and Aaron to hear and see them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r2.anchor: قلت: وهذا كقوله تعالى: {إن الله مع الذين اتقوا والذين هم محسنون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r3.claim: God does not disappoint a supplicant or become distracted from the prayer; He hears supplication. The verse encourages prayer, which is never lost with Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r3.anchor: والمراد من هذا: أنه تعالى لا يخيب دعاء داع، ولا يشغله عنه شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r4.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r4.claim: Salman reports the Prophet’s statement that God is too generous to return a servant’s raised hands empty after the servant asks Him for good. Al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb; some transmitters did not raise it to the Prophet, and other collections transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r4.anchor: عن سلمان -يعني الفارسي -رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r5.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that a Muslim’s lawful prayer, without a break of kinship, receives one of three outcomes: swift fulfillment, preservation for the afterlife, or an equivalent harm averted; the Prophet says God gives abundantly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r5.anchor: عن أبي سعيد: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r6.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r6.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit reports that a Muslim’s prayer is answered or an equivalent harm is kept away, provided it involves neither sin nor breaking family ties.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p506/r6.anchor: عن مكحول، عن جبير بن نفير، أن عبادة بن الصامت حدثهم أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhī grades the report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb by this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r1.anchor: ورواه الترمذي، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الدارمي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that a servant continues to receive an answer so long as he is not impatient, saying, ‘I prayed, but my prayer was not answered.’ The report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r3.claim: Muslim reports that prayer continues to be answered unless it asks for sin or severing kinship, or the servant grows impatient; impatience is repeating that one prayed without seeing an answer, then tiring of prayer and abandoning it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r4.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s statement that a servant remains in a good state unless he becomes impatient, which means saying that he prayed but God did not answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r4.anchor: عن أنس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r5.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha says a believer’s prayer either comes quickly in this life or is stored for the next, unless the person is impatient or despairing; she defines both as saying they asked but received no answer. ʿUrwa narrates her explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r5.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، أنها قالت: ما من عبد مؤمن يدعو الله بدعوة فتذهب، حتى تعجل له في الدنيا أو تدخر له في الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r6.claim: Ibn Qusayṭ says he heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib teach exactly what ʿĀʾisha taught about a prayer’s fulfillment, unless the supplicant is impatient or despairing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r6.anchor: قال ابن قسيط: وسمعت سعيد بن المسيب يقول كقول عائشة سواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s analogy of hearts as vessels, some more receptive than others, and urges people to ask with certainty: God does not answer a servant who calls with a heedless heart.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p507/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r1.speaker: نافع بن معد يكرب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r1.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits an unusual report from Nāfiʿ ibn Maʿd Yakrib: he and ʿĀʾisha asked about the verse, and Gabriel conveyed God’s greeting and promise to answer the sincere servant’s call. Ibn Kathīr calls this route gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r1.anchor: حدثني أبي نافع بن معد يكرب، قال: كنت أنا وعائشة سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r2.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports through Ibn ʿAbbās from Jābir that the Prophet recited the verse and made a long talbiya affirming God’s oneness, the truth of the promise and meeting, Paradise, Hell, the Hour, and resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس: حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r3.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r3.claim: Al-Bazzār reports from Anas through al-Ḥasan that God assigns worship without partners to Himself, recompenses the servant’s deeds, and makes prayer the shared matter whose answer is His part.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r4.claim: Because this encouragement to pray is placed amid the fasting rulings, Ibn Kathīr reads it as urging earnest supplication after completing the fast month and at every ifṭār.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p508/r4.anchor: هذه الآية الباعثة على الدعاء، متخللة بين أحكام الصيام، إرشاد إلى الاجتهاد في الدعاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports that a fasting person has an answered prayer at ifṭār; he would gather his family and children to pray when breaking the fast.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r1.anchor: عن جده عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r2.claim: Ibn Mājah transmits from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr that the fasting person’s supplication at breaking the fast is not refused; Ibn Abī Mulayka heard him ask for forgiveness by God’s all-encompassing mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r2.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r3.claim: The Prophet names three supplications that are not rejected: those of a just ruler, a fasting person until ifṭār, and an oppressed person. The last rises beneath the clouds, heaven’s gates open for it, and God vows to grant help even if delayed; the report appears in Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p509/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr and Qalun from Nafiʿ retain the yāʾ in al-dāʿi and daʿāni in connected reading; other readers omit it, either preserving the original or easing pronunciation with kasra indicating the yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r1.anchor: الداعي إذا دعاني بإثبات الياء فيهما في الوصل أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r2.claim: Ajāba and istajāba both mean to answer; the root denotes cutting, as does the cited j āb ū (they cut) in 89:9, since an answer resolves the questioner's suspense.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r2.anchor: أجاب واستجاب بمعنى، وأصله من الجوب، وهو القطع، ومنه: (جابوا الصخر بالواد (9)

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r3.claim: Rushd is the opposite of error and means attaining good; a rāshid is a soundly guided person.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r3.anchor: والرشد نقيض الغي، والرشد إصابة الخير، ومنه: (رجل رشيد)

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r4.claim: The lām is an imperative and required for third-person commands; with a present addressee it may be omitted or retained, is originally kasra, and may be vowelless after a single letter.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r4.anchor: اللام في قوله: فليستجيبوا لام الأمر، ولا بد منها في الغائب، فأما في الحاضر فيجوز حذفها وإثباتها

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says a questioner asked whether God is near and should be addressed quietly, or far and should be called aloud.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r5.anchor: أقريب وبنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه؟ فنزلت الآية، عن الضحاك

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says some people asked where their Lord was.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r6.anchor: سأل بعضهم: أين ربنا؟ فنزلت الآية، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r7.claim: Qatada says the verse answered people asking how they should invoke God.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r7.anchor: نزلت جوابا لقوم سألوا: كيف ندعوه؟، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews asked Muhammad how their Lord could hear their supplication.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r8.anchor: إن اليهود قالوا: يا محمد، كيف يسمع ربك دعاءنا؟ فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r9.claim: After the discussion of fasting, the passage turns to the supplication associated with it.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r9.anchor: ثم عقب ذكر الصوم بما يلزم من الدعاء

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r10.claim: The question may concern God's location, how to invoke Him, or how to reach His mercy, matching the reported occasions.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r10.anchor: يحتمل عن المكان، ويحتمل كيف ندعوه، ويحتمل عن كيف التوصل إلى رحمته

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r11.claim: Some take the answer to be God's statement that He is near; others take it to be that He answers.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r11.anchor: ومنهم من قال: الجواب في قوله: أجيب والأقرب أن يكون السؤال عن صفته

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r12.claim: The question most likely concerns God's attribute, not His action; an implied 'say' makes the answer 'I am near,' and this rules out spatial location because God would not be near every petitioner if located in a place.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r12.anchor: فيه إضمار، أي فقل: إني قريب يدل بذلك أنه لا مكان له؛ إذ لو كان له مكان لم يكن قريبا من كل من يناجيه

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r13.claim: Other explanations say God is near in answering, quick to answer, in hearing, or in knowledge and power.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: قريب الإجابة، أي سريعها. وقيل: قريب السماع يسمع دعاءهم كسماع القريب

JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r14.claim: The statement means that God answers whoever calls on Him, although its surface form is categorical.
JISHUMI:v1p770#2/r14.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداعي إذا دعان يعني: أجيب دعاء من دعاني، وهذا وإن كان دعوة الداعي ظاهره على القطع

JISHUMI:v1p772/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r1.claim: Prayer has conditions: the petitioner must know God, know what is proper to ask, and know the proper way to make the request.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r1.anchor: فمنهما: معرفة الداعي بربه ليصح أن يوجه الدعاء إليه. ومنها: أن يعرف حسن ما يدعو، وما لا يحسن

JISHUMI:v1p772/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r2.claim: When the conditions hold, God answers if answering benefits the petitioner and delays if delay is more beneficial; human welfare cannot depend on their choice and request.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r2.anchor: فإذا دعا بشرائط الدعاء، وعلم تعالى أن إجابته مصلحة أجاب، وإن كانت المصلحة في التأخير أخر الإجابة

JISHUMI:v1p772/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r3.claim: Supplication is devotional worship; a benefit may be tied to the act of asking and would not be beneficial absent the request.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r3.anchor: أنه يكون تعبدا، ولأنه يجوز أن تكون المصلحة في فعله عند مسألتهم، ولولا سؤالهم لم يكن فعله مصلحة

JISHUMI:v1p772/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r4.claim: The command means that people should yield to God's commands and prohibitions; istajāba and ajāba are synonymous.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r4.anchor: فليستجيبوا يعني فلينقادوا لي فيما أمرتهم به ونهيتهم عنه؛ لأن استجبته واستجبت له بمعنى أجبته

JISHUMI:v1p772/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r5.claim: They must affirm everything God revealed.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r5.anchor: وليؤمنوا بي أي ليصدقوا بجميع ما أنزلته

JISHUMI:v1p772/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r6.claim: Laʿallahum yarshudūn means 'so that they may be guided,' not that God is uncertain; alternatively it urges them to act in hope of guidance.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r6.anchor: أي لكي يرشدوا، وليس هو على الشك، وقيل: افعلوا ذلك متعرضين للرشد

JISHUMI:v1p772/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r7.claim: The verse denies that God occupies a place or direction, since that would make Him not near to every petitioner, refuting anthropomorphists.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r7.anchor: الآية تدل على نفي المكان؛ إذ لو كان في جهة لم يكن قريبا من كل داع فيبطل قول المشبهة

JISHUMI:v1p772/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p772/r8.claim: Abu Ali says the verse praises believers and implies that God answers believers' prayers rather than sinners; Abu Bakr al-Ikhshid allows answering an unbeliever's prayer as a gracious favor.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r8.anchor: عن أبي علي، وجوز أبو بكر الإخشيد

JISHUMI:v1p772/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r9.claim: The unrestricted wording makes turning to God for religious and worldly needs obligatory.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r9.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الانقطاع إليه في منافع الدين والدنيا؛ لأنه لم يفصل

JISHUMI:v1p772/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r10.claim: Believers must trust God's promise, which is why the command to believe follows the promise to answer.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r10.anchor: وتدل على وجوب التصديق والثقة بوعده، فلذلك قال: وليؤمنوا بي عقيب إجابة الدعاء

JISHUMI:v1p772/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r11.claim: God is not known by immediate necessity, since then asking about Him would have no meaning.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r11.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى لا يعرف ضرورة؛ إذ لو كانوا مضطرين لم يكن للسؤال معنى

JISHUMI:v1p772/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r12.claim: The Messenger explains tawḥīd as he explains legal rules, and people ask him about both.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r12.anchor: وتدل على أن الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كما يبين الشرائع يبين التوحيد

JISHUMI:v1p772/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r13.claim: The verse says God intends guidance for all morally responsible people, refuting the Mujbira doctrine of divine will.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r13.anchor: وتدل على أنه أراد من جميع المكلفين الرشد بقوله: لعلهم يرشدون فيبطل قول المجبرة في الإرادة

JISHUMI:v1p772/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p772/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p772/r14.claim: Supplication is worship when it fulfills its conditions.
JISHUMI:v1p772/r14.anchor: وتدل على أن الدعاء عبادة إذا وقع بشرائطه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r1.claim: God’s nearness represents how easily and quickly He answers callers’ needs, like someone nearby who promptly responds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r1.anchor: تمثيل لحاله في سهولة إجابته لمن دعاه وسرعة إنجاحه حاجة من سأله بحال من قرب مكانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r2.claim: The expression is compared with the statement that God is nearer to a person than the jugular vein.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r2.anchor: حبل الوريد ﴾ ق 16 وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r3.claim: The Prophet said that God is between people and the necks of their riding animals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r3.anchor:
وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام
92 ( هو بينكم وبين اعناق رواحلكم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r4.speaker: أعرابي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r4.claim: A Bedouin asked the Prophet whether their Lord was near, so they should speak quietly, or far, so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r4.anchor: قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r5.claim: People should answer God when He calls them to faith and obedience, just as He answers when they call on Him for their needs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r5.anchor: اذا دعوتهم للإيمان والطاعة كما اني اجيبهم اذا دعوني لحوائجهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r6.claim: The final verb is read with the shīn vowel either opened or kasra-marked.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p255/r6.anchor: قرىء ( يرشدون ويرشدون ) بفتح الشين وكسرها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r1.claim: Hasan al-Basri says the verse followed the question whether God is near for private conversation or far so people must call aloud.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنها نزلت في سائل سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : يا محمد أقريب ربنا فنناجيه , أم بعيد فنناديه ؟ فأنزلت هذه الآية , وهو قول الحسن البصري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r2.speaker: عطاء، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r2.claim: Ata and al-Suddi say people asked at what time they should call on God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنها نزلت في قوم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أي ساعة يدعون الله فيها , وهذا قول عطاء والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r3.claim: Qatada says the verse answered people who asked how they should pray.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنها نزلت جوابا لقوم قالوا : كيف ندعو ؟ , وهذا قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r4.claim: Mujahid says that after hearing the command to call on God, people asked where to call Him; the command is 40:60.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r4.anchor: والرابع : أنها نزلت في قوم حين نزل قوله تعالى : { ادعوني أستجب لكم } قالوا : إلى أين ندعوه ؟ , وهذا قول مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r5.claim: One interpretation is that God is near to answering supplication.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r6.claim: The other interpretation is that God is near to hearing supplication.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r7.claim: One explanation takes 'I answer' to mean 'I hear': hearing is expressed as answering because it precedes an answer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r7.anchor: معناه أسمع دعوة الداعي إذا دعاني , فعبر عن السماع بالإجابة , لأن السماع مقدمة الإجابة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r8.claim: Alternatively, God grants a request only when it accords with welfare; a request contrary to welfare cannot be granted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنه أراد إجابة الداعي إلى ما سأل , ولا يخلو سؤال الداعي أن يكون موافقا للمصلحة أو مخالفا لها , فإن كان مخالفا للمصلحة لم تجز الإجابة إليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r9.claim: For a request aligned with welfare, the supplicant may either fulfill or fall short of the conditions for asking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r9.anchor: وإن كان موافقا للمصلحة , فلا يخلو حال الداعي من أحد أمرين : إما أن يكون مستكملا شروط الطلب أو مقصورا فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r10.claim: One view says response is obligatory when conditions are complete because supplication is worship whose reward is an answer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أنها واجبة لأنها تجري مجرى ثواب الأعمال , لأن الدعاء عبادة ثوابها الإجابة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r11.claim: The opposing view says answering is not obligatory: supplication is a request, so granting it is a favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r11.anchor: والثاني : أنها غير واجبة لأنها رغبة وطلب , فصارت الإجابة إليها تفضلا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r12.claim: When the supplicant falls short of the conditions, an answer is not obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r12.anchor: وإن كان مقصورا في شروط الطلب لم تجب إجابته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r13.claim: Whether an answer to an incompletely conditioned request is permitted is disputed: it is barred by the view requiring an answer when conditions are complete, but allowed by the other view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r13.anchor: وفي جوازها قولان : أحدهما : لا تجوز

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r14.claim: Abu Ubayda says istijaba means the same as ijaba, that is, to answer; the poetic proof continues in the next segment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p242/r14.anchor: أحدها : أن الإستجابة بمعنى الإجابة , يقال استجبت له بمعنى أجبته , وهذا قول أبي عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r1.claim: Ka'b ibn Sad's line uses istajaba in the sense of answering, supporting Abu Ubayda's interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r1.anchor: وداع دعا : يا من يجيب إلي الندا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r2.speaker: ثعلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r2.claim: Tha'lab says istijaba means seeking to conform to the answer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن الإستجابة طلب الموافقة للإجابة , وهذا قول ثعلب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r3.claim: A third interpretation is: let them obey Me.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r3.anchor: والثالث : أن معناه فليستجيبوا إلي بالطاعة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p243/r4.claim: A fourth interpretation is: let them call upon Me.

MUQATIL:2:186/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:186/r1.claim: Under the first fasting rule, food, drink, and sex became forbidden after the night prayer or after sleeping before praying it, just as during the day.
MUQATIL:2:186/r1.anchor: أن الرجل إذا صلى العشاء الآخرة، أو نام قبل أن يصليها، حرم عليه الطعام

MUQATIL:2:186/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:186/r2.claim: ʿUmar had sex with his wife after praying ʿishāʾ, regretted it, and confessed to Muhammad, asking whether he could have a dispensation.
MUQATIL:2:186/r2.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب، رضى الله عنه، صلى العشاء الآخرة، ثم جامع امرأته

MUQATIL:2:186/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:2:186/r3.claim: The Prophet told ʿUmar he had not been justified in what he did; ʿUmar returned saddened.
MUQATIL:2:186/r3.anchor: النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم:لم تك جديرا بذلك يا عمر، فرجع حزينا

MUQATIL:2:186/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:186/r4.claim: Sarma ibn Anas worked in his garden, came home exhausted, fell asleep before eating, and woke to find food forbidden; he said fasting had worn him down.
MUQATIL:2:186/r4.anchor: ورأى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم صرمة بن أنس بن صرمة بن مالك

MUQATIL:2:186/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:186/r5.claim: After Muslim men confessed to similar conduct and asked how to repent, God revealed the passage, assuring them of His nearness and response to prayer.
MUQATIL:2:186/r5.anchor: واعترف رجال من المسلمين عند ذلك بما كانوا يصنعون بعد العشاء

MUQATIL:2:186/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:186/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:186/r6.claim: God is near in answering; “let them respond to Me” means obey, and “believe in Me” means affirm Him, so they may be guided.

BURSEVI:v1p241/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241/r1.claim: Yahya al-Barmaki supported Sufyan al-Thawri with a thousand dirhams monthly; Sufyan prayed that God cover Yahya's afterlife, and a companion later dreamed Yahya said he was forgiven through Sufyan's prayer.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r1.anchor: وكان يحيى البرمكي يجري على سفيان الثوري كل شهر ألف درهم وكان سفيان يدعو له في سجوده

BURSEVI:v1p241/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r2.speaker: الصائب
BURSEVI:v1p241/r2.claim: A verse by al-Ṣāʾib urges lighting a lamp for the world's dark days so that one has a lamp at the grave, illustrating good deeds that benefit in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r2.anchor: تيره روزان جهانرا براغي درياب تاس ازمرك ترا شمع مزاري باشد

BURSEVI:v1p241/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241/r3.claim: After commanding the fast, observing its count, and urging takbīr and gratitude, God adds this verse to assure them He knows their state, hears their remembrance and speech, answers prayers, and rewards deeds.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r3.anchor: لما أمرهم بصوم الشهر ومراعاة العدة وحثهم على القيام بوظائف التكبير والشكر عقبه بهذه الآية

BURSEVI:v1p241/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r4.speaker: أعرابي
BURSEVI:v1p241/r4.claim: An Arab Bedouin asked the Prophet whether their Lord was near, so they could whisper to Him, or far, so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed to answer.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r4.anchor: وسبب النزول ما روي أن أعرابيا قال لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه

BURSEVI:v1p241/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241/r5.claim: God's nearness means closeness in knowledge and encompassing awareness, a metaphor for His full knowledge of people's acts and states, not spatial proximity, which would place Him near some and far from others.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r5.anchor: فهو تمثيل لكمال علمه بأفعال العباد وأقوالهم واطلاعه على أحوالهم

BURSEVI:v1p241/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r6.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
BURSEVI:v1p241/r6.claim: Abu Musa reports that as the Prophet and companions approached Khaybar, they shouted takbīr in a valley; the Prophet told them they were calling One who hears, is near, and is with them, not a deaf or absent one.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r6.anchor: قال أبو موسى الأشعري لما توجه رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إلى خيبر أشرف الناس على واد فرفعوا أصواتهم بالتكبير

BURSEVI:v1p241/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241/r7.claim: Loud prayer suits the heedless by driving away stray thoughts, while subdued prayer suits people present with God.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r7.anchor: وهذا باعتبار المشارب والمقامات واللائق بحال أهل الغفلات الجهر لقلع الخواطر كما أن المناسب لأهل الحضور الحفاء

BURSEVI:v1p241/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241/r8.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p241/r8.claim: Bursevī introduces a Saʿdī couplet after contrasting prayer styles; the couplet continues in the next segment.
BURSEVI:v1p241/r8.anchor: كما أن المناسب لأهل الحضور الحفاء ، قال السعدي :

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r1.claim: The promise to answer supplication further establishes the figurative nearness intended here.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r1.anchor: تقرير للقرب المجازي المراد في هذا المقام وهو الحالة الشبيهة بالقرب المكاني

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r2.claim: The verse promises an answer to the supplicant, while apparent unanswered prayers are qualified by 6:41: by God's will, in accordance with decree, not for an impossible request, or when answering is good for the petitioner.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r2.anchor: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r3.claim: God answers the supplicant's call with a response, fulfills the request with what was sought, and meets desperate need with sufficiency.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r3.anchor: والإجابة إعطاء ما سئل والله تعالى يقابل مسألة السائل بالإسعاف ودعاء الداعي بالإجابة

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r4.claim: People should answer God's call to faith and obedience as He answers their calls in their needs.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r4.anchor: إذا دعوتهم للإيمان والطاعة كما أجيبهم إذا دعوني

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r5.claim: استجاب, استجاب له, and أجاب are equivalent; the verb's root carries the sense of cutting off a request by delivering what is sought.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r5.anchor: واستجابه واستجاب له وأجابه واحد قطع مسألته بتبليغة مراده وأصله من الجوب والقطع

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh distinguishes responding as submission and surrender from faith as a heart-quality; the order implies that obedience and worship precede faith's light and strength.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ الاستجابة عبارة عن الانقياد والاستسلام والإيمان عبارة عن صفة القلب

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r7.claim: The reciprocal command displays divine generosity: God, though wholly self-sufficient, answers people, so people in every way dependent on Him should answer His call.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r7.anchor: أنا أجيب دعاءك مع أني غني عنك مطلقا فكن أنت أيضا مجيبا لدعائي مع أنك محتاج إلي من كل الوجوه

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r8.claim: Righteous guidance means reaching sound interests in religion and worldly life; those who respond and believe attain such interests.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r8.anchor: راجين إصابة الرشد وهو الاهتداء لمصالح الدين والدنيا

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r9.claim: The sharia and Sufi path censure failing to ask God to remove distress, as if resisting Him or claiming one can endure His hardships; a Mathnawī couplet says supplication remedies calamity.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r9.anchor: اعلم أن عدم الدعاء بكشف الضر مذموم عند أهل الشريعة والطريقة

BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r10.claim: Bursevī quotes the first half of a Mathnawī couplet about calamity and supplication; its second half continues in the next segment.
BURSEVI:v1p241#2/r10.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : تافرود آيد بلا بي دافعي

BURSEVI:v1p242/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r1.claim: The second half of the Mathnawī couplet says that without supplication there is no remedy when calamity falls.

BURSEVI:v1p242/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r2.claim: Taking practical means is obligatory for ordinary people and beginners in the path; trust is better for intermediates, while perfected saints regard trust and taking means as equal.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r2.anchor: فالتسبب واجب للعوام والمبتدعين في السلوك

BURSEVI:v1p242/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r3.speaker: إبراهيم الخليل
BURSEVI:v1p242/r3.claim: When Gabriel met Abraham in the air as he was thrown into the fire and offered help, Abraham said he needed nothing from Gabriel and that God's knowledge of his state sufficed; this is the perfected mystic's station of annihilation and subsistence in God.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r3.anchor: روي أن إبراهيم الخليل عليه السلام لما ألقي في النار لقيه جبريل

BURSEVI:v1p242/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r4.claim: The Prophet tailored his guidance to people's stations: he told a Bedouin who left his camel loose to tie it and trust God, while some are urged to the birds' trust when not settled in prior decree.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r4.anchor: وقد كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يكلم الناس بقدر مراتبهم

BURSEVI:v1p242/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r5.claim: A divine answer to prayer is certain, but answering the call differs from granting the requested thing: God says ‘At your service’; fulfillment may come now, later, in the Hereafter, or as something better.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r5.anchor: فإن إجابة الدعوة غير قضاء الحاجة وقضاء الحاجة غير إجابة الدعوة

BURSEVI:v1p242/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r6.speaker: عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p242/r6.claim: A report says a Muslim's prayer is not rejected except when it asks for sin or severing kinship; otherwise its good may be stored for the Hereafter or evil averted in proportion to the prayer.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث "دعوة المسلم لا ترد إلا لإحدى ثلاث

BURSEVI:v1p242/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r7.claim: Answering is also conditioned on the servant answering God's call to obedience, as the next clause says.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r7.anchor: ومنها أنه شرط لهذه الإجابة إجابة العبد إياه فيما دعاه إليه

BURSEVI:v1p242/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r8.claim: Supplication has conditions and courtesies that cause an answer; one who neglects them commits excess and does not merit a response.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r8.anchor: ومنها أن للدعاء شرائط وآدابا وهي أسباب الإجابة

BURSEVI:v1p242/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p242/r9.claim: Among the special conditions is purifying the supplicant, beginning with bodily purification through lawful food; a proverb calls lawful food the teeth of supplication's key to heaven.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r9.anchor: فعليه أن يزكي البدن أو لا فيصلحه بلقمة الحلال

BURSEVI:v1p242/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p242/r10.speaker: عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p242/r10.claim: The Prophet describes a dusty traveler raising his hands to God while his food, drink, clothes, and nourishment are unlawful, and asks how such a prayer could be answered.
BURSEVI:v1p242/r10.anchor: عليه السلام : "الرجل يطيل السفر يمد يده إلى السماء أشعث أغبر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r1.speaker: أعرابي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r1.claim: An Arab asked whether their Lord was near so they could speak privately or far so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r1.anchor: ولما قال اعرابى لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه نزل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r2.claim: God is near in knowledge and answering prayer, not spatial location, since He is exalted above being located.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r2.anchor: علما واجابة لتعاليه عن القرب مكانا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r3.speaker: سهل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r3.claim: Sahl and Yaʿqūb retain the yāʾ of daʿānī both in pause and continuation; Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ other than Qālūn do so in continuation, while the rest omit it in both.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r3.anchor: الداعي دعانى فى الحالين سهل ويعقوب ووافقهما أبو عمرو ونافع غير قالون فى الوصل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r4.claim: God’s promise to answer prayer is true and unfailing, but answering a prayer differs from granting the requested need.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r4.anchor: ثم إجابة الدعاء وعد صدق من الله لا خلف فيه غير أن إجابة الدعوة تخالف قضاء الحاجة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r5.claim: Answering is God’s ‘At your service, My servant’ when a believer calls; granting the request may be immediate, delayed, in the hereafter, or replaced by what is better.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r5.anchor: فاجابة الدعوة أن يقول العبد يا رب فيقول الله لبيك عبدى وهذا أمر موعود موجود لكل مؤمن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r6.claim: They should respond when God calls them to faith and obedience, just as He answers when they call Him with their needs.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r6.anchor: إذا دعوتهم للايمان والطاعة كما انى أجيبهم إذا دعونى لحوائجهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r7.claim: The lām in ‘let them believe in Me’ is an imperative particle.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r8.claim: Laʿalla expresses hope that they attain right guidance, the opposite of error.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p91#2/r8.anchor: ليكونوا على رجاء من إصابة الرشد وهو ضد الغى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r1.claim: If people ask about the One they worship, tell them He is near, rewards obedience, answers the supplicant, and knows a servant's fasting, prayer, and other deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r1.anchor: المعنى وإذا سألوك عن المعبود فأخبرهم أنه قريب يثيب على الطاعة ويجيب الداعي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r2.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse followed Umar's intercourse with his wife after the night prayer, his regret and tears, and his report to the Prophet before the concession was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r2.anchor: فقال مقاتل: إن عمر رضي الله عنه واقع امرأته بعدما صلى العشاء فندم على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r3.claim: Another account links the verse to people who ate after sleeping, contrary to the initial rule, then regretted it; the verse signaled repentance's acceptance and abrogation of that rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r3.anchor: وقيل: لما وجب عليهم في الابتداء ترك الأكل بعد النوم فأكل بعضهم ثم ندم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Jews asked how their Lord could hear prayer if heaven was five hundred years away and each heaven equally thick; the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r4.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال: قالت اليهود كيف يسمع ربنا دعاءنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says people asked whether their Lord was near, so they could whisper, or far, so they must call loudly; the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: سببها أن قوما قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أقريب ربنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r6.speaker: عطاء وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r6.claim: Ata and Qatada say that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked at what time they should call upon God, prompting this verse.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r7.claim: One explanation is that God is near in answering prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r7.anchor: فإني قريب } أي بالإجابة. وقيل بالعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r8.claim: Another explanation is that God is near through His knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r8.anchor: وقيل بالعلم. وقيل: قريب من أوليائي بالإفضال والإنعام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r9.claim: A further explanation is that God is near to His friends through favor and beneficence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r9.anchor: وقيل: قريب من أوليائي بالإفضال والإنعام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r10.claim: Here supplication means worship and God's answering means acceptance of the worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r10.anchor: أي أقبل عبادة من عبدني فالدعاء بمعنى العبادة، والإجابة بمعنى القبول.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r11.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r11.claim: Abu Dawud transmits from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir the Prophet's statement that supplication is worship, followed by the command to call on God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r11.anchor: دليله ما رواه أبو داود عن النعمان بن بشير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r12.claim: The phrase in 40:60 about those too proud of worship refers to those too proud to supplicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r12.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r13.claim: God commands and encourages supplication, names it worship, and promises to answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r13.anchor: فأمر تعالى بالدعاء وحض عليه وسماه عبادة، ووعد بأن يستجيب لهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r14.claim: A report from Ubada ibn al-Samit says this community, like the prophets, was promised an answer to prayer; it also contrasts their roles concerning hardship and witness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186/r14.anchor: روى ليث عن شهر بن حوشب عن عبادة بن الصامت قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r1.speaker: خالد الربعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r1.claim: Khalid al-Rab'i marvels that God commands supplication and promises an answer without stating a condition, unlike promises tied to faith and good works or sincere worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r1.anchor: وكان خالد الربعي يقول: عجبت لهذه الأمة في { ادعوني أستجب لكم } أمرهم بالدعاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r2.claim: Earlier communities turned to their prophets to ask God for their needs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r2.anchor: وكانت الأمم تقرع إلى أنبيائها في حوائجهم حتى تسأل الأنبياء لهم ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r3.claim: The promise to answer does not require every supplicant to receive every specific thing requested.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r3.anchor: لا يقتضي الاستجابة مطلقا لكل داع على التفصيل، ولا بكل مطلوب على التفصيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r4.claim: God says He does not love transgressors; al-Qurtubi counts anyone persisting in a major sin, knowingly or unknowingly, among them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r4.anchor: وكل مصر على كبيرة عالما بها أو جاهلا فهو معتد، وقد أخبر أنه لا يحب المعتدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r5.claim: Some scholars understand the promise as God answering if He wills, as stated in 6:41, so the unrestricted wording is qualified elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: أجيب إن شئت كما قال: فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r6.claim: The Prophet supplicated for three things, received two, and was denied one; al-Qurtubi says details will follow in al-An'am.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r6.anchor: وقد دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ثلاث فأعطي اثنتين ومنع واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r7.claim: Another view says the verse generally tells believers that their Lord answers supplications, hears them, knows their distress, and responds as He wills.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنما مقصود هذا الإخبار تعريف جميع المؤمنين أن هذا وصف ربهم سبحانه أنه يجيب دعاء الداعين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r8.claim: The contrast is with calling on beings besides God who cannot respond.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r8.anchor: ومن أضل ممن يدعو من دون الله من لا يستجيب له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r9.claim: A master may answer a servant or a parent a child without granting the specific request, so answering and granting are distinct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r9.anchor: وقد يجيب السيد عبده والوالد ولده ثم لا يعطيه سؤله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r10.claim: Some form of answer necessarily occurs when prayer is made, since these are un-abrogated declarative statements and otherwise God would be a liar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#2/r10.anchor: لأن أجيب وأستجب خبر لا ينسخ فيصير المخبر كذابا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying that whoever is granted openness in supplication has the doors of response opened for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r1.anchor: من فتح له في الدعاء فتحت له أبواب الإجابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r2.claim: A revelation to David says God has bound Himself to answer anyone who calls, but if He answers wrongdoers, He curses them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r2.anchor: وأوحى الله تعالى إلى داود: أن قل للظلمة من عبادي لا يدعوني فإني أوجبت على نفسي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r3.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r3.claim: One view says every prayer is answered in one of three ways: granted now, stored for the afterlife, or offset by equivalent protection from harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الله يجيب كل الدعاء فإما أن تظهر الإجابة في الدنيا، وإما أن يكفر عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r4.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reports that a Muslim who asks without sin or severing kin receives one of three outcomes; when asked if they should ask more, the Prophet replied that God is more generous.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r4.anchor: ما من مسلم يدعو بدعوة ليس فيها إثم ولا قطيعة رحم إلا أعطاه الله بها إحدى ثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r5.speaker: أبو محمد عبد الحق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r5.claim: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq graded the Abu Sa'id report sound; Abu Umar says it appears in the Muwatta with a disconnected chain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r5.anchor: وصححه أبو محمد عبد الحق، وهو في الموطأ منقطع السند.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r6.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r6.claim: Abu Umar presents the report as a connected exegesis of God's promise to answer in 40:60, with all three outcomes counting as response.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r6.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وهذا الحديث يخرج في التفسير المسند لقول الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says every servant who prays is answered: worldly provision is granted if it is allotted to him, otherwise it is stored for him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كل عبد دعا أستجيب له فإن كان الذي يدعو به رزقا له في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r8.claim: Muslim's report from Abu Hurayra adds that prayer continues to be answered unless the supplicant asks for sin or severing kin, or becomes impatient and gives up.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r8.anchor: لا يزال يستجاب للعبد ما لم يدع بإثم أو قطيعة رحم ما لم يستعجل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r9.claim: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Abu Dawud transmit from Abu Hurayra that a person remains answered unless he hastens, saying he prayed without receiving an answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r9.anchor: وروى البخاري ومسلم وأبو داود عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r10.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r10.claim: Scholars offer two readings of the answer promise: a necessary outcome among the three already mentioned, or the possibility of the specific request being granted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r10.anchor: قال علماؤنا رحمة الله عليهم: يحتمل قوله «يستجاب لأحدكم» الإخبار عن وجوب وقوع الإجابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r11.claim: On the first reading, saying that no answer came denies all three outcomes and empties the supplication of each.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r11.anchor: بطل وقوع أحد هذه الثلاثة الأشياء وعري الدعاء من جميعها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r12.claim: On the second reading, impatience prevents a specific answer because it shows despair, weak certainty, and discontent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r12.anchor: ويمنع من ذلك قول الداعي: قد دعوت فلم يستجب لي لأن ذلك من باب القنوط

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r13.claim: Unlawful food and its like also prevent a supplication from being answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#3/r13.anchor: قلت: ويمنع من إجابة الدعاء أيضا أكل الحرام وما كان في معناه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r1.claim: The Prophet describes a traveler who raises his hands and calls on God while eating, drinking, wearing, and being nourished with unlawful things, then asks how such a prayer could be answered.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r1.anchor: الرجل يطيل السفر أشعث أغبر يمد يديه إلى السماء يا رب يا رب ومطعمه حرام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r2.claim: The hadith's question expresses how unlikely acceptance is for someone in that condition; answering requires conditions in the supplicant, prayer, and requested thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r2.anchor: وهذا استفهام على جهة الاستبعاد من قبول دعاء من هذه صفته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r3.claim: The supplicant must know that only God can meet the need and that all intermediaries are under His control.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r3.anchor: أن يكون عالما بأن لا قادر على حاجته إلا الله، وأن الوسائط في قبضته ومسخرة بتسخيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r4.claim: The supplicant needs sincere intent and an attentive heart; God does not answer a heedless, distracted heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r4.anchor: وأن يدعو بنية صادقة وحضور قلب، فإن الله لا يستجيب دعاء من قلب غافل لاه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r5.claim: Other conditions on the supplicant are avoiding unlawful food and not tiring of supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r5.anchor: وأن يكون مجتنبا لأكل الحرام، وألا يمل من الدعاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r6.claim: The requested matter must be legally permissible to ask for and do; the cited report excludes sin and severing kinship, which includes Muslims' rights and wrongs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r6.anchor: ومن شرط المدعو فيه أن يكون من الأمور الجائزة الطلب والفعل شرعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r7.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r7.claim: Sahl al-Tustari lists seven conditions: humility, fear, hope, persistence, reverence, generality, and lawful food.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r7.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله التستري: شروط الدعاء سبعة: أولها التضرع والخوف والرجاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r8.claim: Ibn Ata likens supplication to a structure with pillars, wings, causes, and times: when these fit, it gains strength, ascends, and succeeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء: إن للدعاء أركانا وأجنحة وأسبابا وأوقاتا فإن وافق أركانه قوي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r9.claim: Ibn Ata names the pillars as presence of heart, compassion, resignation, and humility; sincerity is its wings, pre-dawn its time, and blessings on Muhammad its cause.
