QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r9.anchor: فأركانه حضور القلب والرأفة والاستكانة والخشوع، وأجنحته الصدق، ومواقيته الأسحار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r10.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r10.claim: Another account gives four conditions: guarding the heart in solitude, tongue among people, eyes from the forbidden, and stomach from unlawful food.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r10.anchor: وقيل: شرائطه أربع أولها حفظ القلب عند الوحدة، وحفظ اللسان مع الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r11.claim: Some say supplication must be free of grammatical solecism, as a poem says a lion who calls his Lord with solecism gets no answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r11.anchor: أن يكون سليما من اللحن كما أنشد بعضهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r12.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r12.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham explains unanswered prayers by listing disobedience, failure to follow the Prophet and Qur'an, ingratitude, neglect of the afterlife, complicity with Satan, lack of preparation for death, and preoccupation with others' faults.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r12.anchor: وقيل لإبراهيم بن أدهم: ما بالنا ندعو فلا يستجاب لنا؟ قال: لأنكم عرفتم الله فلم تطيعوه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r13.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r13.claim: Ali tells Nawf that God instructed David to require pure hearts, humble eyes, and clean hands from worshippers, and said He would not answer anyone while they wronged another creature.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r13.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه لنوف البكالي: يا نوف، إن الله أوحى إلى داود أن مر بني إسرائيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r14.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r14.claim: Ali warns Nawf against being a poet, tax official, police officer, collector, or customs collector; David's night prayer excluded those jobs and players of the tambourine or drum.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r14.anchor: يا نوف، لا تكونن شاعرا ولا عريفا ولا شرطيا ولا جابيا ولا عشارا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r15.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r15.claim: Scholars say a supplicant should not qualify requests for forgiveness, mercy, or gifts with if You wish; he should ask decisively as someone in need.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r15.anchor: قال علماؤنا: ولا يقل الداعي: اللهم أعطني إن شئت، اللهم اغفر لي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r16.claim: Adding if You wish suggests indifference to God's mercy or gift, like asking someone whose help one does not need; the needy should be resolute.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r16.anchor: وأيضا فإن في قوله: «إن شئت» نوع من الاستغناء عن مغفرته وعطائه ورحمته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r17.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to make one's request resolutely and not say grant it if You wish, since no one can compel God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r17.anchor: روى الأئمة واللفظ للبخاري عن أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r18.claim: The Muwatta also quotes the wording, O God forgive me if You wish and have mercy on me if You wish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#4/r18.anchor: اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت، اللهم ارحمني إن شئت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r1.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r1.claim: Scholars say resolving to ask means striving in supplication and hoping for an answer, without despairing of God's mercy, since one asks the Generous.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r1.anchor: قال علماؤنا: قوله «فليعزم المسألة» دليل على أنه ينبغي للمؤمن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r2.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says knowledge of one's own faults should not deter prayer: God answered Iblis when he asked to be delayed until resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r2.anchor: قال سفيان ابن عيينة: لا يمنعن أحدا من الدعاء ما يعلمه من نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r3.claim: Likely times and circumstances for answered supplication include pre-dawn, breaking the fast, between call and commencement of prayer, Wednesday afternoon, distress, travel, illness, rain, and battle ranks.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r3.anchor: وللدعاء أوقات وأحوال يكون الغالب فيها الإجابة، وذلك كالسحر ووقت الفطر، وما بين الأذان والإقامة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r4.speaker: أم الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r4.claim: Umm al-Darda told Shahr ibn Hawshab to pray when he felt goosebumps, saying prayer is answered then.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r4.anchor: وروى شهر بن حوشب أن أم الدرداء قالت له: يا شهر، ألا تجد القشعريرة؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r5.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r5.claim: Jabir says the Prophet prayed three times at the Conquest Mosque on Monday and Tuesday and was answered on Wednesday between prayers; Jabir sought that hour for grave troubles and recognized the answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r5.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله: دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسجد الفتح ثلاثا يوم الإثنين ويوم الثلاثاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r6.speaker: أبو رجاء الخراساني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r6.claim: Abu Raja al-Khurasani interprets the command as let them pray to Me.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r6.anchor: قال أبو رجاء الخراساني: فليدعوا لي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets it as let them request that I answer; this is the usual seeking sense of the form استفعل, apart from exceptional forms such as istaghna Allah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: المعنى فليطلبوا أن أجيبهم. وهذا هو باب «استفعل» أي طلب الشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r8.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r8.claim: Mujahid and others understand it as answering God's call to faith, obedience, and action.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المعنى فليجيبوا إلي فيما دعوتهم إليه من الإيمان أي الطاعة والعمل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r9.claim: Ajaba and istajaba are synonymous; the cited line uses istajaba in the sense of answering.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r9.anchor: ويقال: أجاب واستجاب بمعنى ومنه قول الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r10.claim: The sīn is extra and the lām is an imperative; it jussives the verb because it makes it future-only, like a conditional particle, or because it only precedes verbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r10.anchor: والسين زائدة واللام لام الأمر. وكذا «وليؤمنوا» وجزمت لام الأمر لأنها تجعل الفعل مستقبلا لا غير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r11.claim: Rushd is the opposite of error; the source gives two pronunciations and forms meaning guidance, direction, or the straightest road.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r11.anchor: والرشاد خلاف الغي. وقد رشد يرشد رشدا. ورشد بالكسر يرشد رشدا، لغة فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r12.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r12.claim: Al-Jawhari records marashid as routes' destinations, arshad as the straighter road, rashda as legitimate birth, Umm Rashid as a mouse's nickname, and Banu Rashdan as an Arab clan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r12.anchor: والمراشد: مقاصد الطرق. والطريق الأرشد: نحو الأقصد. وتقول: هو لرشدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r13.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r13.claim: Al-Harawi says rushd, rushd, and rashad mean guidance and uprightness, which explains the verse's hope that they will be guided.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:186#5/r13.anchor: وقال الهروي: الرشد والرشد والرشاد: الهدى والاستقامة ومنه قوله: «لعلهم يرشدون».

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.claim: After the fasting rulings, magnification, and gratitude, God's nearness assures worshippers that He knows their remembrance, hears their call, answers prayer, and does not disappoint hope.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r1.anchor: بين أنه سبحانه بلطفه ورحمته قريب من العبد مطلع على ذكره وشكره فيسمع نداءه ، ويجيب دعاءه ، ولا يخيب رجاءه

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.claim: The order places praise before supplication, as Abraham first praised God and then prayed; Razi compares this sequence with Abraham's words.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r2.anchor: تنبيها على أن الدعاء لا بد وأن يكون مسبوقا بالثناء الجميل

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r3.claim: One proposed connection is that the earlier strict rule barring food after sleep led some fasting people to disobey, repent, and ask about acceptance; this verse announced acceptance and lifted that severity.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r3.anchor: ثم ندموا وسألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن توبتهم ، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية مخبرا لهم بقبول توبتهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r4.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r4.claim: Kaʿb reports that Moses asked whether God was near for private conversation or far for calling; God said He accompanies those who remember Him and should be remembered in every state.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r4.anchor: عن كعب أنه قال ، قال موسى عليه السلام : يا رب أقريب أنت فأناجيك ، أم بعيد فأناديك

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r5.speaker: أعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r5.claim: A Bedouin asked the Prophet whether their Lord was near so they could speak privately or far so they should call aloud, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r5.anchor: أن أعرابيا جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : أقريب ربنا فنناجيه ، أم بعيد فنناديه

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r6.claim: During an expedition, when companions raised their voices in remembrance and supplication, the Prophet said they were calling One who hears and is near, not a deaf or absent being.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r6.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : ( إنكم لا تدعون أصم ولا غائبا إنما تدعون سميعا قريبا )

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r7.speaker: قتادة وغيره
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r7.claim: Qatada and others say the companions asked the Prophet how they should call upon God, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r7.anchor: ما روي عن قتادة وغيره أن سببه أن الصحابة قالوا : كيف ندعو ربنا يا نبي الله

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r8.speaker: عطاء وغيره
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r8.claim: Ata and others say the companions asked at what hour they should pray to God, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r8.anchor: قال عطاء وغيره : إنهم سألوه في أي ساعة

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews of Medina asked Muhammad how their Lord could hear their supplication, prompting the revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r9.anchor: ما ذكره ابن عباس ، وهو أن يهود أهل المدينة قالوا : يا محمد كيف يسمع ربك دعاءنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's companions asked where their Lord was, and the verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r10.anchor: قال الحسن : سأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا : أين ربنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r11.claim: Another proposed occasion repeats the fasting account: after eating following sleep, people repented and asked whether their repentance would be accepted, so this verse was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p80#2/r11.anchor: ثم إنهم أكلوا ثم ندموا وتابوا وسألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تعالى هل يقبل توبتنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r1.claim: The question about God could concern His essence, attributes, or actions: spatial nearness, whether and how He hears or permits supplication, or whether He grants what is requested.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r1.anchor: فذلك السؤال إما أنه كان سؤالا عن ذات الله تعالى ، أو عن صفاته ، أو عن أفعاله

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r2.claim: An essence-focused question would come from someone who allows anthropomorphic comparison and asks about nearness or distance in relation to God's essence.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r2.anchor: فيسأل عن القرب والبعد بحسب الذات

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r3.claim: An attribute-focused question might ask whether God hears prayer, which names may be used, or whether prayer may be offered in any manner; Razi cites the instruction about moderate prayer volume.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r3.anchor: وأما السؤال عن الصفات فهو أن يكون السائل سأل عن أنه تعالى هل يسمع دعاءنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r4.claim: An action-focused question could ask whether God answers after hearing a supplication and fulfills the request.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r4.anchor: وأما السؤال عن الأفعال فهو أن يكون السائل سأل الله تعالى أنه إذا سمع دعاءنا فهل يجيبنا إلى مطلوبنا

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r5.claim: Razi favors the essence-focused reading because the wording 'about Me' appears to ask about God's own essence rather than an action.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r5.anchor: إلا أن حمله على السؤال عن الذات أولى لوجهين الأول : أن ظاهر قوله : { عني } يدل على أن السؤال وقع عن ذاته

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r6.claim: A vague question followed by a specific answer indicates that the question concerned that specific matter; the answer about nearness therefore supports a question about proximity and distance.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r6.anchor: السؤال متى كان مبهما والجواب مفصلا ، دل الجواب على أن المراد من ذلك المبهم هو ذلك المعين

RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r7.claim: A counterreading takes the question to concern God's action—whether He answers and fulfills requests—because the statement about nearness is followed by a promise to answer prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p81/r7.anchor: بل السؤال كان على الفعل ، وهو أنه تعالى هل يجيب دعاءهم ، وهل يحصل مقصود ، بدليل أنه لما قال : { فإني قريب }

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r1.claim: God's nearness here is not spatial; it means nearness through knowledge and preservation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r1.anchor: أن هذا القريب ليس قربا بحسب المكان

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r2.claim: If God occupied a place and were perceptible, He would be divisible; dependence on parts would make Him possible and originated, which is impossible for the eternal Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r2.anchor: في المكان مشارا إليه بالحس لكان منقسما

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r3.claim: A spatial occupant must be infinite in all directions, infinite in only some, or finite throughout; the first two are impossible and the third is rejected by both sides, so God is not in a direction.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r3.anchor: فبطل القول بأنه تعالى في الجهة

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r4.claim: The verse says God is near to all; a spatial being would be near some and far from others, such as people east and west, proving this nearness is not directional.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r4.anchor: فلما دلت الآية على كونه تعالى قريبا من الكل علمنا أن القرب المذكور في هذه الآية ليس قربا بحسب الجهة

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r5.claim: Nonspatial nearness means that God hears supplications, sees pleading, and is near through knowledge and preservation; Razi compares this with God's being with people and nearer than the jugular vein.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r5.anchor: ثبت أن المراد منه القرب بمعنى أنه تعالى يسمع دعاءهم ويرى تضرعهم ، أو المراد من هذا القرب : العلم والحفظ

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r6.claim: When Muslims say God is everywhere, Razi explains that they mean His governance, preservation, and guardianship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r6.anchor: والمسلمون يقولون إنه تعالى بكل مكان ويريدون به التدبير والحفظ والحراسة

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r7.claim: The answer suits questions about where God is, whether He hears, how loudly to pray, whether He grants requests, and whether He accepts repentance; it is near in each relevant sense.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r7.anchor: فثبت أن هذا الجواب مطابق للسؤال على جميع التقديرات

RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r8.claim: Razi allows that some questioners may have been anthropomorphists, as such views occurred among Arab polytheists, Jews, and others.
RAZI-FULL:v5p82/r8.anchor: فقد كان في مشركي العرب وفي اليهود وغيرهم من هذه طريقته

RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r1.claim: When events occur in accordance with a supplicant's aim, this indicates a world-governing agent who hears prayer; otherwise the desired result would not occur at that time.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r1.anchor: إنما يعرف بحدوث تلك الأشياء على وفق غرض الداعي فدل على أنه لولا مدبر لهذا العالم يسمع دعاءه

RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r2.claim: The Creator causes possible essences to exist, so He is a mediator between each essence and its existence and is nearer to it than it is to itself.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r2.anchor: فكان إيجاد الصانع كالمتوسط بين ماهيات الممكنات وبين وجوداتها فكان الصانع أقرب إلى ماهية كل ممكن

RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r3.claim: More deeply, the Creator causes each essence to be what it is—substance, blackness, intellect, or soul—so He is nearer to each essence than it is to itself.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r3.anchor: فهو أيضا لأجله كان الجوهر جوهرا

RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r4.claim: Against the claim that an essence cannot be made itself, Razi argues that the same reasoning would make existence and predication uncaused, absurdly implying that nothing is caused; thus everything is caused by an agent.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r4.anchor: فإذن لم يقع شيء ألبتة بالفاعل ، وذلك باطل ظاهر البطلان ، فإذن وجب الحكم بأن الكل بالفاعل

RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r5.claim: Abu Amr and Qalun from Nafi retain the yāʾ in الداعي and إذا in connected recitation; the other readers omit it, with the first retention for connection and the second for lightening.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع { الداعى * إذا } بإثبات الياء فيهما في الوصل والباقون بحذفها

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r1.claim: Al-Khattabi derives duʿāʾ as the verbal noun of calling, used as a noun like 'sound'; its reality is a servant's seeking divine care and aid.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي : الدعاء مصدر من قولك : دعوت الشيء أدعوه دعاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r2.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r2.claim: Some opponents argue that prayer is useless: if the requested outcome is known to God, it must occur; if not, it cannot occur.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعض الجهال الدعاء شيء عديم الفائدة ، واحتجوا عليه من وجوه أحدها : أن المطلوب بالدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r3.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r3.claim: They argue that all events must ultimately follow from the eternal necessary cause; what it eternally wills is inevitable and what it does not will is impossible, so prayer cannot affect fixed destinies.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r3.anchor: فكل ما اقتضى ذلك المؤثر القديم وجوده اقتضاء قديما أزليا كان واجب الوقوع ، وكل ما لم يقتض

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r4.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r4.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet states that God decreed the measures before creating creation by a specified number of years; opponents cite it to argue that prayer cannot change destiny.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r4.anchor: وربما عبروا عن هذا الكلام بأن قالوا : الأقدار سابقة والأقضية متقدمة والدعاء لا يزيد فيها

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r5.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that the pen has dried concerning what will be, offered as support for the claim that prayer has no effect.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r5.anchor: وروي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال : ( جف القلم بما هو كائن )

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that lifespan, provision, creation, and creation are already settled; the source repeats the last term as الخلق.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r6.anchor: وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قال : ( أربع قد فرغ منها : العمر والرزق والخلق والخلق )

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r7.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r7.claim: They argue that God's knowledge of hidden things makes asking unnecessary, citing His knowledge of furtive eyes and concealed hearts; they also claim Gabriel's highest devotion came from not asking.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r7.anchor: أنه سبحانه علام الغيوب : { يطاع يعلم خائنة الاعين وما تخفى الصدور }

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r8.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r8.claim: They say an absolutely generous God will provide whatever benefits a servant, while requesting what is not beneficial is impermissible.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r8.anchor: فالجواد المطلق لا يهمله وإن لم يكن من مصالحه

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r9.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r9.claim: They argue that the highest station is contentment with God's decree and that supplication conflicts with it by preferring one's own wish and seeking personal advantage.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r9.anchor: أجل مقامات الصديقين وأعلاها الرضا بقضاء الله تعالى والدعاء ينافي ذلك لأنه اشتغال بالإلتماس

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r10.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r10.claim: They claim prayer resembles giving orders or prohibitions, which they regard as bad manners toward a generous, merciful Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r10.anchor: أن الدعاء يشبه الأمر والنهي وذلك من العبد في حق المولى الكريم الرحيم سوء أدب

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r11.claim: A divine saying transmitted through the Prophet promises a greater gift to one whom remembrance keeps from asking; opponents use it to favor leaving supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r11.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال رواية عن الله سبحانه وتعالى : ( من شغله ذكري عن مسألتي

RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r12.speaker: بعض الجهال
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r12.claim: From these arguments, the opponents conclude that leaving supplication is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v5p83#2/r12.anchor: قالوا فثبت بهذه الوجوه أن الأولى ترك الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r1.speaker: الجمهور الأعظم من العقلاء
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r1.claim: The great majority of rational thinkers hold that supplication is among the most important stations of servitude, supported by revelation and reason.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r1.anchor: وقال الجمهور الأعظم من العقلاء : إن الدعاء أهم مقامات العبودية ، ويدل عليه وجوه من النقل والعقل

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r2.claim: As scriptural evidence, Razi lists questions about the Spirit, mountains, and the Hour, and questions on practical matters including spending, sacred months, wine and gambling, orphans, menstruation, spoils, Dhul-Qarnayn, truth, and inheritance.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r2.anchor: وأما الفروعية فمنها في البقرة على التوالي

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r3.claim: Razi distinguishes answers preceded by 'say,' one preceded by an immediate-response particle, and this verse's direct divine answer without 'say.'
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r3.anchor: هذه الأسئلة جاءت أجوبتها على ثلاثة أنواع فالأغلب فيها أنه تعالى لما حكى السؤال قال لمحمد : قل

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r4.claim: The mountains question is foundational, so God says to answer immediately; delay would leave doubt about an essential doctrine. The answer that mountains will be pulverized follows because each part can be destroyed, hence the whole can.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r4.anchor: كأنه قال يا محمد أجب عن هذا السؤال في الحال ولا تؤخر الجواب فإن الشك فيه كفر

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r5.claim: Other listed questions concern subsidiary matters, so their answers do not use the immediate-response particle.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r5.anchor: أما سائر المسائل فهي فروعية فلا جرم لم يذكر فيها فاء التعقيب

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r6.claim: This verse omits 'say,' indicating the special dignity of prayer: there is no intermediary between God and the servant while supplicating.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r6.anchor: كأنه سبحانه وتعالى يقول عبدي أنت إنما تحتاج إلى الواسطة في غير وقت الدعاء أما في مقام الدعاء فلا واسطة بيني وبينك

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r7.claim: The wording assigns the servant to God and God to the servant: 'My servants ask about Me' and 'I am near.'
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r7.anchor: أن قوله : { وإذا سألك عبادي عني } يدل على أن العبد له وقوله : { فإني قريب } يدل على أن الرب للعبد

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r8.claim: The verse says God is near to the servant, not that the servant is near to God: a contingent being is rooted in nonexistence and cannot approach God by itself, but God draws near through grace and mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r8.anchor: فلا يمكنه القرب من الرب أما الحق سبحانه فهو القادر من أن يقرب بفضله وبرحمته من العبد

RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r9.claim: Prayer brings nearness when the caller becomes absorbed in knowledge of the One and turns from all else; attention to personal aims obstructs nearness, making supplication the best worship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p84/r9.anchor: فثبت أن الدعاء يفيد القرب من الله ، فكان الدعاء أفضل العبادات

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.claim: A second proof of prayer's excellence is God's command to call upon Him with a promise to answer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.anchor: الحجة الثانية في فضل الدعاء : قوله تعالى : { وقال ربكم ادعونى أستجب لكم }

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r2.claim: A third proof is that God censures people whose hearts hardened and who did not humble themselves when affliction came, indicating the importance of turning to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r2.anchor: أنه إذا لم يسأل يغضب فقال

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r3.claim: The Prophet instructs a supplicant to ask firmly for forgiveness rather than say 'if You will,' since no one can compel God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r3.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يقول أحدكم : اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت ولكن يجزم فيقول : اللهم اغفر لي

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r4.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet calls supplication the marrow of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r4.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( الدعاء مخ العبادة )

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r5.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r5.claim: Al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir reports the Prophet's saying that supplication is worship; Razi explains it as the greatest or best part, like pilgrimage being identified with standing at Arafat as its chief pillar.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r5.anchor: وعن النعمان بن بشير أنه عليه السلام قال : ( الدعاء هو العبادة ) وقرأ

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r6.claim: A fourth proof is the commands to call on God humbly and privately and the statement that people would mean nothing to God without their supplication; denying prayer denies the Qur'an.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية }

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r7.claim: Razi calls the first objection contradictory: if prayer's result is already known to occur, refuting prayer is pointless; if it is known not to occur, denial is unnecessary.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r7.anchor: أنها متناقضة ، لأن إقدام الإنسان على الدعاء إن كان معلوم الوقوع فلا فائدة في اشتغالكم بإبطال الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r8.claim: God's knowledge and decree exceed human understanding; divine wisdom keeps servants between hope and fear, validating religious duties despite God's encompassing knowledge and decree.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r8.anchor: والحكمة الإلهية تقتضي أن يكون العبد معلقا بين الرجاء وبين الخوف اللذين بهما تنم العبودية

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r9.speaker: الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r9.claim: The companions asked whether deeds were already decreed or newly determined; the Prophet replied that they were decreed, then told them to act because each person is eased toward what he was created for.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r9.anchor: ولهذا الإشكال سألت الصحابة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا : أرأيت أعمالنا هذه أشيء قد فرغ منه

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r10.claim: Razi says the report holds people to both prior decree and action: it does not cancel outward work, whose performance is itself decreed and facilitated during life.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r10.anchor: فلم يعطل ظاهر العمل بما يفيد من القضاء والقدر ، ولم يترك أحد الأمرين للآخر

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r11.claim: The same applies to earning and provision: they are settled in principle and are neither increased by seeking nor reduced by leaving them.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r11.anchor: وكذا القول في باب الكسب والرزق فإنه مفروغ منه في الأصل لا يزيده الطلب ولا ينقصه الترك

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r1.claim: Prayer does not inform God; it displays servitude, humility, brokenness, and total return to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r1.anchor: ليس المقصود من الدعاء الإعلام ، بل إظهار العبودية والذلة والانكسار والرجوع إلى الله بالكلية

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r2.claim: Something not initially beneficial may become beneficial in light of a prior supplication.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r2.anchor: أنه يجوز أن يصير ما ليس بمصلحة مصلحة بحسب سبق الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r3.claim: If supplication expresses humility and is followed by acceptance of God's decree, it is among the highest stations; this also answers the remaining objections.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r3.anchor: إذا كان مقصوده من الدعاء إظهار الذلة والمسكنة ثم بعد رضى بما قدره الله وقضاه ، فذلك أعظم المقامات

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.claim: Although promises to answer prayer appear unqualified in these verses, Razi says a further verse qualifies them: God removes what is invoked only if He wills, and the general wording is read in light of that qualification.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.anchor: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r5.claim: Every supplicant receives something: the requested outcome when it accords with decree, or otherwise inner calm, an open heart, and patience to bear present hardship; this too is an answer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r5.anchor: وعلى كل حال فلا يعدم فائدة ، وهو نوع من الاستجابة

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r6.claim: Al-Qaffal transmits from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri a Prophetic report that a Muslim's prayer is answered by quick fulfillment, a store for the afterlife, or an equivalent evil averted, unless it asks for sin or severing kinship; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r6.anchor: ما روى القفال في تفسيره عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( دعوة المسلم لا ترد إلا لإحدى ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r1.claim: God’s promise to answer prayer need not mean an immediate answer; fulfillment even in the afterlife makes the promise true.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r1.anchor: فإذا استجاب له ولو في الآخرة كان الوعد صدقا

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r2.claim: A genuine petitioner must know God; otherwise he calls an imagined nonexistent object rather than God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r2.anchor: فثبت أن الشرط الداعي أن يكون عارفا بربه

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r3.claim: Knowing that divine action accords with decree, knowledge, and wisdom makes an absolute demand incoherent; the request is implicitly conditional on that wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r3.anchor: ومن صفات الرب سبحانه أن لا يفعل إلا ما وافق قضاءه وقدره وعلمه وحكمته

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r4.claim: One possible sense of supplication is affirming God’s oneness and praising Him; calling its acceptance an answer matches the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r4.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون الدعاء عبارة عن التوحيد والثناء على الله

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī takes أجيب to mean “I hear”; hearing and answering are closely linked, as in “God hears whoever praises Him.”
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري : { أجيب } ههنا بمعنى أسمع لأن بين السماع

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r6.claim: Supplication can mean repentance, since a repentant person calls upon God; its answer then means acceptance of repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r6.anchor: وثانيها : أن يكون المراد من الدعاء التوبة عن الذنوب ، وذلك لأن التائب

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r7.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that supplication is worship, supporting the interpretation of الدعاء as worship.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r7.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الدعاء هو العبادة ) ومما يدل عليه قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r8.claim: If supplication means worship, God’s answer is fulfillment of the reward promised to the obedient; verses 40:60 and 42:26 support this reading.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r8.anchor: فإجابة الله تعالى للدعاء بهذا التفسير عبارة عن الوفاء بما ضمن للمطيعين من الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r9.claim: If supplication means asking for needs, the original question applies; the other three interpretations remove the difficulty.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86/r9.anchor: فالسؤال المذكور إن كان متوجها على هذا التفسير لم يكن متوجها على التفسيرات الثلاثة المتقدمة

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r1.claim: The Muʿtazila restrict answered prayer to believers free of grave sin: being called answered is a great religious honor, incompatible with a sinner’s deserved disgrace; a sinner’s request may occur without counting as an answer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r1.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : قالت المعتزلة : { أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان } مختص بالمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r2.claim: God answers despite being wholly self-sufficient, while servants respond despite total need; this asymmetry displays divine generosity.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r2.anchor: المسألة الأولى : وجه الناظم أن يقال : إنه تعالى قال : أنا أجيب دعاءك مع أني غني

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r3.claim: God does not condition His answer on the servant answering first, so divine response is prior grace rather than payment for obedience; this refutes the Muʿtazila’s claim.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r3.anchor: لأنه لو قال ذلك لصار لدعائي ، وهذا تنبيه على أن إجابة الله عبده فضل منه ابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r4.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says أجاب and استجاب are synonyms; Kaʿb al-Ghanawī’s verse illustrates استجاب for answering a caller.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r4.anchor: المسألة الثانية : قال الواحدي : أجاب واستجاب بمعنى واحد : قال كعب الغنوي

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r5.speaker: أهل المعنى
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r5.claim: The servant’s response to God is obedience, while God’s response to a servant is granting the requested thing; each responds in a fitting way.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r5.anchor: وقال أهل المعنى : الإجابة من العبد لله الطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r6.claim: If responding to God means assent of heart and tongue, it is faith, making “respond to Me and believe in Me” seem redundant.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r6.anchor: / المسألة الثالثة : إجابة العبد لله إن كانت إجابة بالقلب واللسان ، فذاك هو الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r7.claim: If responding means acts of obedience, faith precedes those acts, so the expected order would be “believe in Me, then respond”; al-Rāzī raises the inversion as a question.
RAZI-FULL:v5p86#2/r7.anchor: وإن كانت إجابة العبد لله عبارة عن الطاعات كان الإيمان مقدما على الطاعات
